THE AIRCRAFT TOUCHED DOWN ON THE MAIN GEAR FOR INITIAL ROLLOUT. UPON SUFFICIENT LOSS OF SPEED, THE NOSE SETTLED ON THE PARTLY EXTENDED NOSE GEAR, WHICH SUBSEQUENTLY COLLAPSED. THE AIRCRAFT STOPPED ON THE RUNWAY WITH DAMAGE TO THE PROPELLER, NOSE GEAR STRUT AND SLIGHT DAMAGE TO THE LOWER ENGINE COWL. THERE WERE NO INJURIES TO THE PIC OR HIS STUDENT. HE STATED THE SAME INFORMATION AS WHAT I HAD RECEIVED FROM THE TYLER POUNDS FIELD TOWER. THE PILOT ^PRIVACY DAT^ STATED THAT HE WOULD BE SUBMITTING AN NTSB FORM 8020-1/2. I THEN CONTACTED ^PRIVACY DATA OMIT^ OF JOHNSON AVIATION AND MADE ARRANGEMENTS TO LOOK AT THE AIRCRAFT ON 01/20/2005. ON 01/20/2005 I ARRIVED AT JOHNSON AVIATION AND BEGAN INVESTIGATING N23PD FOR DAMAGE. IT WAS APPARENT IMMEDIATELY THAT TUBE, BEECHCRAFT P/N 169-820022-1, WAS BROKEN AT THE FORWARD ROD END, (P/N 169-380082-1). IT WAS NOT APPARENT AS TO IF THE TUBE ASSEMBLY WAS BROKEN PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT OR UPON CONTACT WITH THE RUNWAY. IT WAS THEN DECIDED THAT WE WOULD CONDUCT A GEAR RETRACTION TEST TO SEEE IF THE PROBLEM COULD BE REPEATED. THE AIRCRAFT WAS PLACED ON AIRCRAFT JACKS AND THE LANDING GEAR RETRACTED. THE GEAR RETRACTED NORMALLY AND APPEARED TO EXTEND NORMALLY WITH NO FORWARD AIR PRESSURE PLACED ON THE NOSE GEAR ASSEMBLY. IT WAS THEN DECIDED TO TRY TO SIMULATE THE PROBLEM BY APPLYING RESISTANCE TO THE NOSE GEAR ASSEMBLY DURING THE EXTENSION PHASE. UPON APPLYING RESISTANCE BY HOLDING THE NOSE GEAR REARWARD, IT WAS FOUND THAT THE NOSE GEAR COULD BE PREVENTED FROM EXTENDING AND THE HYDRAULIC PUMP OF THE POWER PACK WOULD NOT SHUT OFF AFTER SUFFICIENT PRESSURE WAS BUILT UP AND THE MOTOR WOULD CONTINUE TO RUN. IT IS BELIEVED THAT EITHER THE HYDRAULIC ACTUATOR FOR THE NOSE GEAR OR THE POWER PACK ASSEMBLY WAS BYPASSING FLUID, WHICH WILL NOT ALLOW SUFFICIENT PRESSURE TO EXTEND THE NOSE GEAR OR SHUT OFF THE PUMP ROTOR. THE FLUID LEVEL IN THE POWERPACK WAS AT THE FULL LEVEL.

20050405014299I	(-23) AS REPORTED BY MOLINE ATCT, ON APRIL 5, 2005, MESABA FLIGHT #3637 REPORTED A NUMBER ONE ENGINE FIRE WARNING ILLUMINATED AFTER DEPARTURE AT APPROXIMATELY 200' AGL. THIS CAUSES THE MANIFOLD FUEL NOZZLES TO LOOSEN DURING HI-POWER ENGINE OPERATION (TAKE-OFF AND CLIMB) RESULTING IN FUEL SPRAYING INTO THE ENGINE COWL. THIS FUEL IS IGNITED AND THE RESULTING FIRE CAUSED THE FIRE WARNING ILLUMINATION. TO DATE REDUCING ENGINE POWER HAS EXTINGUISHED THE FLAMES BUT THE POTENTIAL FOR A CATASTROPHIC EVENT IS EVIDENT.

THE AIRCRAFT THEN FELL BACKWARDS AND IMPACTED THE GROUND TAIL FIRST AT IMPACT IN A WOODED AREA APPROXIMATELY 1500' WEST OF THE RUNWAY. THE DIRECTION OF TRAVEL AT IMPACT WAS 040 DEGREES MAGNETIC HOWEVER, THE NOSE OF THE AIRCRAFT WAS IN THE DIRECTION OF 220 DEGREES. THERE WAS NO FIRE. NO PREEXISTING DAMAGE WAS NOTED. THE PILOT'S BODY WAS IN THE LEFT SEAT AND THE SEAT BACK AND SHOULDER HARNESS ATTACHMENTS WERE BROKEN. BOTH FUEL CAPS WERE SECURED. NO FUEL WAS NOTED IN THE RIGHT TANK. THE LEFT WING CONTAINED APPROXIMATELY 6-8 US GALLONS OF AUTO FUEL. THE FUEL SELECTOR WAS LOCATED BETWEEN THE "BOTH" AND "LEFT" POSITION. THE MANUFACTURER OF THE FUEL SELECTOR WAS ANTARE. THIS FUEL SELECTOR HAS THREE PORTS AND FOUR POSITIONS. THE THREE PORTS ARE "LEFT, RIGHT AND BOTH". THE FOUR POSITIONS ARE "LEFT, RIGHT, BOTH AND OFF." THE "RIGHT" FUEL TANK FEED LINE WAS ATTACHED TO THE "BOTH" PORT. IF THE SELECTOR HANDLE IS ALLOWED TO ROTATE TO THE POSITION BETWEEN "BOTH" AND "LEFT" THE FUEL OUTPUT LINE FROM THE SELECTOR VALVE IS CONNECTED TO BOTH THE RIGHT AND LEFT FUEL TANK. WITH ONLY FUEL IN THE LEFT TANK THE HIGH PRESSURE ELECTRIC FUEL PUMPS COULD DRAW AIR ONLY FROM THE RIGHT TANK AND NO FUEL. THE DETENTS IN THE SELECTOR VALVE ARE VERY WEAK AND ALMOST UNNOTICEABLE. THERE WAS AN UNNECESSARY VENT LINE FROM THE FUEL SUMP TANK CONNECTED TO THE TOP OF THE LEFT TANK. UNDER CONDITIONS OF AN UNCOORDINATED TURN OR SLIP THIS COULD ALLOW AIR TO ENTER THE FUEL FEED LINES TO THE FUEL PUMPS. THE SHAPE OF THE FUEL SUMP TANK IS SUCH (WIDE AND LOW) THAT DURING AN UNCOORDINATED TURN OR SLIP WITH A PARTIALLY FILLED SUMP TANK, THE FUEL FEED LINE TO THE ENGINE MAY BECOME UNCOVERED. SEE ATTACHED DRAWINGS OF THE FUEL SYSTEM INSTALLED BY ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ AND THE DRAWING OF THE RECOMMENDED FUEL SYSTEM FOR A PUSHER TYPE AIRCRAFT.

THE PILOT'S WRITTEN STATEMENT SAID HE EXECUTED A 180-DEGREE TURN AND MADE THE TURN FINE, BUT DID NOT HAVE ENOUGH ALTITUDE TO CLEAR A 40-FOOT TREE LINE TO LAND BACK AT HIS GRASS STRIP. THE LOCAL AUTHORITIES AND THE CRASH, FIRE, AND RESCUE RESPONDED TO THE ACCIDENT SITE. FAA INSPECTORS INSPECTED THE AIRCRAFT ENGINE, WHICH REVEALED NO ABNORMALITY. THE AIRCRAFT FUEL SYSTEM WAS INSPECTED WHICH REVEALED THAT THE FUEL TANK WAS INTERNALLY CORRODED WITH RUSTED METAL FLAKES AND SEDIMENT ON THE BOTTOM OF THE FUEL TANK. THIS CAUSED THE ENGINE TO POSSIBLY STARVE OF FUEL WHEN THE RUSTED METAL PARTICLES BLOCKED THE AN822-5 FITTING EXITING THE FUEL TANK TO THE AIRCRAFT'S FUEL SELECTOR VALVE. THE INSPECTORS STARTED THE AIRCRAFT ENGINE, WHICH VERIFIED THE ENGINE MAGNETO WAS OPERATING. VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS PREVAILED AT THE TIME, AND NOF FLIGHT PLAN WAS FILED. THE AIRCRAFT RECEIVED SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE. THE PILOT WAS NOT INJURED.

20050630034149A	(-23) THE PILOT STATED THAT THE ENGINE QUIT AT ABOUT 250 FEET AGL DURING HIS CLIMB-OUT AFTER TAKE-OFF. HE STATED THAT HE LEVELED THE AIRCRAFT AND THE ENGINE RESTARTED. HE FELT THAT IT MIGHT HAVE MOMENTARILY STARTED DURING THE TRANSITION FROM CLIMB TO GLIDE AND THEN QUIT FOR GOOD. DUE TO A BILLBOARD LOCATED NEAR THE END OF THE RUNWAY AND HIS LOW ALTITUDE, THE PILOT ELECTED TO LAND IN THE GRASS MEDIAN ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF THE INTERSTATE THAT PARALLELED THE RUNWAY. DURING THE LANDING, HE HIT A STAND OF SAPLINGS WITH THE RIGHT WING. THE AIRCRAFT IMPACTED THE GROUND AT A LOW AIRSPEED AND FLIPPED OVER. THE AIRCRAFT RECEIVED SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE AND THE PILOT SUSTAINED MINOR INJURIES IN THE ACCIDENT. AN INSPECTION OF THE ENGINE AND ITS ACCESSORIES REVEALED NO OBVIOUS PROBLEMS. FOLLOWING INSPECTIONS OF THE FUEL SYSTEM, FUEL WAS ADDED TO THE LEFT FUEL TANK AND A NEW PROPELLER WAS INSTALLED. THE ENGINE WAS STARTED AND RAN WITH NO PROBLEMS NOTED. RESPONDING POLICE OFFICERS AND WITNESSES ON THE SCENE CONFIRMED THAT THERE WAS NO SMELL OF FUEL AT THE SCENE. A CHECKOF THE FUEL TANKS AT THE IMPOUND FACILITY REVEALED NO VISIBLE FUEL IN THE TANKS. THE FUEL CAPS USED CURVED TUBING FOR VENTING. BOTH VENTS WERE OPEN AND CLEAR WITH NO SIGN OF INSECT ACTIVITY. A FUEL SAMPLE TAKEN FROM THE FUEL FILTER BOWL REVEALED THAT 100LL AVIATION GRADE FUEL WAS IN USE. THE FUEL SAMPLE WAS CLEAR AND BRIGHT WITH NO WATER. THE CARBURETOR FUEL SCREEN WAS INSPECTED WITH NO CONTAMINATION FOUND. TWENTY-FOUR OUNCES OF FUEL WERE DRAINED FROM THE LEFT FUEL TANK. THE RIGHT FUEL TANK SUMP WAS DAMAGED IN THE CRASH, SO NO FUEL COULD BE DRAINED FROM THAT TANK. THE FUEL PICKUPS ARE LOCATED IN THE LOWER CENTER PORTION OF THE INBOARD END OF EACH WING TANK. WHEN FUEL WAS ADDED TO THE LEFT WING TANK, IT TOOK TWO GALLONS OF FUEL, WITH THE AIRCRAFT SITTING ON THE GROUND IN A NORMAL POSITION, BEFORE ANY FUEL FLOWED FROM THE FUEL TANK PICKUP. BASED ON THIS FINDING, IT IS ESTIMATED THAT THE AIRCRAFT WOULD HAVE REQUIRED A MINIMUM OF 2.5-3.5 GALLONS OF FUEL IN EACH TANK FOR A SAFE TAKE-OFF (CAP. IS APPROX. 6.5 GAL PER TANK FOR A TOTAL CAPACITY OF 13 GALS.). THE PILOT STATED THAT HE HAD CHECKED THE FUEL TANKS BEFORE TAKE OFF, BUT COULD NOT BE CERTAIN OF THE QUANTITY OF FUEL ACTUALLY IN THE TANKS. BASED ON THE REPORTED FLIGHT TIME SINCE THE LAST TOP-OFF OF THE AIRCRAFT'S FUEL TANKS, (APPROX. 1.5 HOURS) THE AIRCRAFT WOULD HAVE HAD NO MORE THAN 6 GALLONS (APPROX. 3 GAL. IN EACH TANK) OF FUEL LEFT ONBOARD WHEN THE ACCIDENT FLIGHT BEGAN. NO ACCURATE FUEL QUANTITY INDICATION SYSTEM IS INSTALLED IN THE AIRCRAFT. THE PILOT HAD ONLY OWNED THE AIRCRAFT FOR TWO DAYS PRIOR TO THE CRASH. A TELEPHONE INTERVIEW REVEALED THAT THE PREVIOUS OWNER ALWAYS KEPT THE TANKS TOPPED OFF, SO MOST TAKEOFFS WERE ACCOMPLISHED WITH FULL TANKS. OCCASIONALLY, A TAKEOFF WOULD BE MADE AFTER AN HOURS' FLIGHT. THE PREVIOUS OWNER REPORTED THAT HE HAD NEVER ENCOUNTERED ANY TYPE OF FUEL PROBLEM.

A SECOND WITNESS WAS DRIVING NORTH ON HIGHWAY 83, WHEN HE NOTICED AN AIRPLANE WAS "COMING UP BEHIND HIM AND LOW." "THE AIRPLANE (LOOKED) LIKE HE TOOK A LEFT TURN, WENT INTO A RAVINE AND (I) DIDN'T SEE HIM UNTIL HE WAS TRYING TO BRING (THE) AIRPLANE UP THE CLIFF." THE WITNESS ALSO NOTED THAT THE AIRPLANE'S LEFT WING "CLIPPED A TREE" BEFORE IMPACTING THE GROUND. SEVERAL FAMILY MEMBERS, WHO WERE VISITING FROM A FOREIGN COUNTRY, WERE DRIVING NORTH ON HIGHWAY 83, AND SAW THE ACCIDENT AIRPLANE ON THE TAXIWAY AT JCT. AFTER DRIVING A WAYS, ONE OF THE WITNESSES REPORTED THE AIRPLANE "FLEW OVER THE ROAD ABOVE US ONLY ABOUT 100 FEET." THE WITNESS THEN STATED THE AIRPLANE TURNED LEFT AND "WENT DOWN IN THE VALLEY", HE MENTIONED THAT "HE COULD SEE IT COMING UP AT TIMES, THEN IT DISAPPEARED." THE WITNESS THEN STATES THAT HIS GIRLFRIEND SAW "IT HIT A TREE AND THEN FLIP OVER." THE AIRPLANE WAS A 1973 MODEL AERO COMMANDER 112, CONFIGURED FOR A MAXIMUM OF FOUR OCCUPANTS, AND FEATURED A RETRACTABLE LANDING GEAR AND A CONTROLLABLE PITCH PROPELLER. 20050914024069A	(-23) NAVION, N2401T SUSTAINED SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE TO ITS RIGHT WING AND HORIZONTAL STABILIZER AFTER LOSING POWER DURING THE INITIAL CLIMB-OUT FROM LAKE GENEVA AIR ESTATES ON SEPTEMBER 14, 2005 AT 1835 CDT. THE PILOT-IN-COMMAND AND SOLE OCCUPANT OF THE AIRCRAFT, ^PRIVACY DATA OMIT^ WAS NOT INJURED. THE PILOT ^PRIVACY DAT^ REPORTED THAT THE VFR PERSONAL FLIGHT WAS FOR THE PURPOSE OF FLYING TO BURLINGTON WISCONSIN TO GET FUEL FOLLOWED BY A LOCAL FLIGHT WITH A PLANNED RETURN TO LAKE GENEVA AIR ESTATES. THE PILOT ^PRIVACY DAT^ REPORTED THAT HE HAD NOT FLOWN THE AIRPLANE FOR TWO WEEKS PRIOR TO THIS FLIGHT, AND THAT THE AIRCRAFT HAD BEEN PARKED OUTSIDE ON A HILL WITH THE NOSE DOWN TO THE RIGHT. HE STATED THE FUEL TANKS WERE ABOUT HALF FULL DURING THIS PERIOD. THE PILOT ^PRIVACY DAT^ STATED HE DID A COMPLETE PREFLIGHT INSPECTION INCLUDING OBTAINING GAS SAMPLES FROM FOUR POINTS OF THE BELLY OF THE PLANE. HE STATED NO WATER WAS FOUND. THE PILOT ^PRIVACY DAT^ REPORTED THAT WHILE TAXIING FOR TAKEOFF, THE ENGINE ALMOST DIED SO HE INCREASED THE MIXTURE ALL THE WAY AND REGAINED SMOOTH OPERATION. HE STATED DURING THE RUNWAY, THE "MAGS WERE ROUGH" SO HE LEANED THE MIXTURE TO PEAK TEMPERATURE AND RECHECKED THE MAGS AT WHICH TIME THEY WERE SMOOTH. HE STATED HE TAXIED INTO POSITION, HELD THE BRAKES WENT TO FULL RIGHT MIXTURE AND FULL POWER FOR FIVE SECONDS AND THEN RELEASED THE BRAKES. THE PILOT ^PRIVACY DAT^ STATED THE TAKEOFF ROLL WAS NORMAL, HE ROTATED AT 65 MPS AND LIFTED OFF AT ABOUT 80 MPH AND STARTED THE CLIMB. HE REPORTED THAT AT APPROXIMATELY 40 FEET AGL THE ENGINE "WENT FLAT". HE STATED HE PUT THE BOOST PUMP HIGH, THE ENGINE CAUGHT FOR A SECOND AND THEN "WENT FLAT" AGAIN. HE STATED HE CHECKED THE AIRSPEED FOUND IT AT 60 MPH AT WHICH TIME HE LOWERED THE NOSE AND REALIZED THAT HE WOULD NOT CLEAR THE FENCE AT THE END OF THE AIRPORT PROPERTY. HE STATED AS THE AIRCRAFT HIT THE FENCE, THE ENGINE CAME BACK TO FULL POWER. 20051114028189I	(-23) ON 11/14/05 AT APPROXIMATELY 0900 MDT, AIRCRAFT N83RR, A LANCE AIR IV-P, DEPARTED HELENA, MONTANA (HLN) WITH AN IFR FLIGHT PLAN ENROUTE TO GARY INDIANA (GYY), WITH ONLY THE PILOT ON BOARD. ABOUT 15 TO 20 MINUTES INTO THE FLIGHT, CRUISING AT FL250, THE PILOT NOTICED THE ENGINE OIL PRESSURE STARTED TO DROP. THE PILOT SLOWLY BROUGHT THE ENGINE POWER BACK TO IDLE AND FEATHERED THE PROPELLER. HE DECLARED AN EMERGENCY AND WAS CLEARED TO DESCEND AND LAND AT WHEATLAND COUNTY AIRPORT, HARLOWTON, MONTANA (HWQ). THE AIRCRAFT LANDED WITHOUT INCIDENT. THE WALTER ENGINE WAS DISASSEMBLED AND INSPECTED BY A WALTER TECHNICIAN. INVESTIGATION FOUND THAT THE FRONT OIL SCAVENGE HAD FAILED. THE FAILURE OF THE PUMP WAS CAUSED BY A PIECE OF MAGNESIUM LEFT OVER FROM THE CASTING OR MACHINING PROCESS THAT APPARENTLY DIDN'T GET CLEANED OUT OF THE FRONT GEARBOX PRIOR TO ASSEMBLY. IT APPEARS THAT THE PIECE OF METAL LODGED IN THE SCAVENGE PUMP CAUSING IT TO FAIL. WHEN THE PUMP FAILED, THE ENGINE OIL ACCUMULATED IN THE FRONT GEARBOX, THEREBY STARVING THE REAR GEARBOX OF ENGINE OIL. THE ENGINE'S PRIMARY OIL PUMP IS DRIVEN FROM THE REAR GEARBOX, SO AS THE OIL ACCUMULATED UP FRONT, THERE WAS MINIMAL OIL LEFT TO CIRCULATE THROUGH THE PRIMARY OIL PUMP RESULTING IN LOSS OF OIL PRESSURE. A FAA FORM 8010-4 MALFUNCTION OR DEFECT REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED BY THE ENGINE MANUFACTURER. THIS INCIDENT IS CONSIDERED CLOSED.

THE CAUSE OF SUBSEQUENT FAILURES OF THE HYDRAULIC STEERING THE BRAKING SYSTEM WERE NOT POSITIVELY DETERMINED. HOWEVER, FAILURE OF THE FLIGHT CREW TO FOLLOW APPROPRIATE EMERGENCY CHECK LIST PROCEDURES FOLLOWING SHUT DOWN OF THE RIGHT ENGINE RESULTED IN SIGNIFICANT COMPLICATIONS DURING THE EMERGENCY LANDING, AND SUBSEQUENT DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ ADDITIONALLY, INSPECTION OF N41527 REVEALED SEVERAL POTENTIAL AIRWORTHINESS ISSUES ASSOCIATED WITH THE AIRCRAFT. 20060107000779I	(-23) INSTRUCTOR PILOT ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ (PIC) WAS TRAINING PILOT ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ ON AN UPCOMING 135-CHECK RIDE FOR THE BHT-206-L3. UPON COMPLETION OF THE TRAINING FLIGHT BOTH PILOTS OBSERVED BUCKLING DAMAGE TO THE TAILBOOM. THE DAMAGE WAS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 18 INCHES AFT OF THE TAILBOOM TO FUSELAGE MOUNT POINT. THE SKIN BUCKLING IS LOCATED FROM THE 0130 POSITION TO THE 0530 POSITION ON THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE TAILBOOM AND THE 0700 POSITION TO THE 1130 POSITION ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE TAILBOOM. THERE WAS A ONE-INCH LONG CRACK IN THE SHEET-METAL SKIN OF THE TAILBOOM AT THE 1130 POSITION APPROXIMATELY 18 INCHES AFT OF THE MOUNT POINT. THE TRAINING FLIGHT TOOK PLACE LATE IN THE AFTERNOON AT APPROXIMATELY 1545-1600. THE AIRCRAFT HAD JUST ARRIVED FROM BEING REPOSITIONED FROM PNE TO OWD. PRIOR TO THE FLIGHT THE PIC/INSTRUCTOR BRIEFED ON POSITIVE CONTROL TRANSFER PROCEDURES. THE TRAINING FLIGHT CONSISTED OF THE FOLLOWING MANUEVERS: PEDAL TURNS, HOVERS, HOVERING AUTOROTATIONS, AND 2 AUTOROTATIONS ONE TERMINATING AT A HOVER AND ONE AUTOROTATION TERMINATING WITH A RUN ON LANDING. DURING THE AUTOROTATION TERMINATING WITH A RUN ON LANDING THE PIC TOOK OVER THE CONTROLS WITHOUT COMMUNICATING WITH THESTUDENT AT APPROXIMATELY 12 FEET AGL AND COMPLETED THE RUN-ON LANDING. BOTH PILOTS WERE INTERVIEWED AND DID NOT FEEL THERE WERE ANY PERIODS DURING THE FLIGHT THAT WOULD BE CONSIDERED TO HAVE INCURRED A HARD LANDING. THE DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS FOR US HELICOPTERS INC. STATED DURING TELEPHONE INTERVIEWS THAT THE AIRCRAFT HAD ENCOUNTERED SEVERE TURBULENCE DURING THE REPOSITIONING FLIGHT FROM PNE TO OWD AND THAT WAS THE REASON FOR THE TAIL-BOOM DAMAGE. DURING INTERVIEWS WITH ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ THE PILOT WHO REPOSITIONED THE HELICOPTER FROM PNE TO OWD HE STATED HE IS NOT AWARE HOW THE DAMAGE COULD HAVE HAPPENED, THERE WAS NEVER A MENTION OF SEVERE TURBULENCE DURING THE PNE TO OWD TRIP. COMMUNICATION WITH BELL HELICOPTER INDICATES THAT THE DAMAGE APEARS SIMILAR TO PREVIOUS EVENTS THAT OCCURRED A NUMBER OF YEARS BACK. "IT WAS FOUND THAT ALLOWING THE MAIN ROTOR RPM TO DECAY BELOW 70% BEFORE THE SKIDS TOUCH THE GROUND IN A TOUCHDOWN AUTOROTATION CAN INDUCE A "WHIRL MODE" TYPE VIBRATION IN THE TAILBOOM. IF SEVERE ENOUGH, THIS VIBRATION CAN CAUSE COMPRESSION BUCKLING IN THE TAILBOOM SKINS." TO ADDRESS THIS PROBLEM, BELL HELICOPTER ISSUED OPERATIONAL SAFETY NOTICE 206L-84-10, WHICH DESCRIBED THE PHENOMENON AND RECOMMENDED THAT THE SKIDS BE IN GROUND CONTACT BEFORE THE MAIN ROTOR DECAYS BELOW 70% DURING A TOUCHDOWN AUTOROTATION. ALSO, A CAUTION WAS ADDED TO THE 206L-3 FLIGHT MANUAL ADDRESSING THIS ISSUE. THE DAMAGE TO THE TAILBOOM NOTED ON N206PL AT THE COMPLETION OF THE TRAINING MANUEVERS IS CONSISTENT WITH THE OPERATIONAL SAFETY NOTICE 206L-84-10.

THE PILOT STATED THAT HE VISUALLY CHECKED THE FUEL LEVEL BEFORE FLIGHT AND FOUND BOTH TANKS FUELED TO THE SLOTS (18.7 GALLONS PER TANK). HE FURTHER STATED THAT HE FLEW THE ENTIRE FLIGHT WITH THE FUEL SELECTOR ON THE RIGHT TANK. UPON EXPERIENCING FUEL EXHAUSTION, THE PILOT SAID HE ATTEMPTED TO RESTART THE ENGINE, BUT HE DID NOT SWITCH THE FUEL SELECTOR TO THE LEFT TANK. HE DID NOT GET THE ENGINE RESTARTED. THERE WAS A POSSIBLE MITIGATING FACTOR IN THE PILOT'S DECISION TO NOT SWITCH FUEL TANKS. THE INVESTIGATING INSPECTOR FOUND THAT, AFTER THE ACCIDENT, BOTH FUEL GAUGES READ ABOUT 70% FULL DESPITE THE FACT THAT THE RIGHT TANK WAS EMPTY AND THE LEFT TANK WAS ABOUT 50% FULL. THE PILOT MAY HAVE RELIED ON ERRONEOUS FUEL GAUGE READINGS.

AFTER TAKEOFF THE CONDITIONEDAIR WAS SWITCHED FROM THE APU SUPPLY TO ENGINES SUPPLY. WHEN CONDITION AIR WAS SWITCHED FROM APU TO ENGINES THE CREW FAILED TO FOLLOW THE PROCEDURE LISTED IN THE MEL BY CLOSING THE SUPPLY FROM THE APU AND ALLOWING PAC PRESSURE TO REDUCE TO LESS THEN 5 PSI BEFORE OPENING THE SUPPLY FROM THE ENGINES. AS A RESULT THE CREW RECEIVED A "L PACK HI PRESS" CAUTION MESSAGE REQUIRING THEM TO FOLLOW THE QHR PROCEDURES OF REDUCING ENGINE POWER. THIS REDUCTION IN ENGINE POWER PREVENTED THE AIRCRAFT FROM CLIMBING AT A RATE SUFFICIENT TO MEET AIRSPACE AND TERRAIN RESTRICTION. SKW20A NOTIFIED ATC OF THE PAC PROBLEM AND INFORMED THEM THEY WERE NOT ABLE TO EXPEDITE THEIR CLIMB, AS REQUESTED BY ATC, PRIOR TO PENETRATING AIRSPACE WHICH WAS BELOW THE MVA.

MOMENTS LATER A US AIRWAYS COWORKER ENTERED THE JET BRIDGE WITH A SHEARED BOLT IN HIS HAND AND TOLD ^PRIVACY DAT^ TO GET OUT OF THE JET BRIDGE. THE AIRCRAFT WAS IN THE PROCESS OF DISEMBARKING PASSENGERS. OF THE ONE HUNDRED PASSENGERS TWENTY WERE NOT ABLE TO DEPLANE DUE TO THE COLLAPSE OF THE JET BRIDGE. THE TWENTY PASSENGERS AND FIVE CREW WERE DEPLANED FROM THE REAR OF THE AIRCRAFT USING THE MOBILE STAIR TRUCK FROM MASSPORT FIRE/RESCUE. WITHIN A FEW MINUTES A COMMAND GROUP WAS ESTABLISHED AND AN ACTION PLAN WAS FORMULATED. IT WAS DECIDED THAT A CRANE NEEDED TO BE EMPLOYED TO LIFT THE JET BRIDGE TO A POINT WHERE THEY COULD MOVE THE AIRCRAFT AWAY FROM THE JET BRIDGE WITHOUT CAUSING FURTHER DAMAGE. A 185-TON CRANE FROM SHAUNESSY CRANE SERVICE IN SOUTH BOSTON, RESPONDED TO THE AIRPORT ALONG WITH A RIGGING TEAM TO MAKE THE LIFT. THE CRANE ARRIVED AT THE AIRPORT AT 1136 EST. SHAUNESSY INC., ASSESSED THE SCENE AND A BRIEFING ON THE DETAILS OF THE LIFT WAS CONDUCTED WITH THE COMMAND GROUP. THE LIFT BEGAN AT 1333L AND WAS COMPLETE INCLUDING REMOVAL OF THE AIRCRAFT AT 1343 EST. THE EXTENT OF THE DAMAGE WAS LIMITED TO JUST THE L-1 DOOR. NO DAMAGE TO ANY OTHER AIRCRAFT STRUCTURE WAS FOUND. THE CAUSE OF THE JET BRIDGE FAILURE WAS THOUGHT TO BE A MALFUNCTIONING JACKSCREW DRIVE CHAIN, STUCK CONTACTOR ON THE LEFT MOTOR OR A BROKEN LIMIT SWITCH (S) ON THE RIGHT STABILIZER BUT FURTHER INVESTIGATION WILL BE NEEDED TO BE CERTAIN AS TO THE ACTUAL CAUSE. AT 1426 EST THE JET BRIDGE WAS SECURED ON A MAINTENANCE STAND AND ALL UNITS SECURED WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE RIGGING CREW AND THE CRANE. THEY SECURED THEIR EQUIPMENT, AND WERE ESCORTED OFF THE AIR OPERATIONS AREA (AOA) AT 1551 EST. INSPECTORS STATEMENT: IT APPEARS AT THIS POINT IN THE INVESTIGATION THAT THE CHAIN THAT IS CONNECTED TOTHE MOTOR THAT RAISES AND LOWERS THE JET BRIDGE SHEARED AND WHEN IT DID THE MOTOR (SELF LEVELING DEVICE) COULD NO LONGER CONTROL THE JET BRIDGE. THERE ARE SAFETY SWITCHES IN THE MOTOR BUT ONCE THE CHAIN SEPARATED THE JACKSCREW ON THE RIGHT SIDE WAS FREE TO MOVE AND IT WENT ALL THE WAY UP WHILE THE LEFT JACKSCREW AND CHAIN REMAINED DOWN. THIS CAUSED ALL EIGHT BOLTS TO SHEAR CAUSING THE TWO WHEELS C

THE GEAR SYSTEM ON THE CESSNA 310 IS MECHANICAL AND DEVELOPS A GREAT AMOUNT OF TORQUE. THE GEAR MOTOR WILL CONTINUE TO RUN UNTIL THE LIMIT SWITCHES ARE CLOSED OR SOMETHING BREAKS. IN THIS CASE WHEN THE NOSE GEAR STUCK ON THE GEAR DOOR BRACKETS, THE MOTOR CONTINUED TO PULL UNTIL THE IDLER BELLCRANK BROKE. AFTER THE BELLCRANK BROKE, THE MOTOR CONTINUED TO RETRACT THE MAIN LANDING GEAR NORMALLY. AT THIS POINT THE NOSE GEAR FELL BACK DOWN IN THE SLIPSTREAM WHERE IT REMAINED UNTIL LANDING. WHEN THE GEAR WAS SELECTED DOWN, THE MAINS CAME DOWN NORMALLY BUT THE PUSHROD THAT WAS NO LONGER ATTACHED TO THE BROKEN IDLER BELLCRANK PENETRATED THE BULKHEAD AT FUSELAGE STATION 19.0 INSTEAD OF PASSING THROUGH THE NORMAL GUIDE HOLE IN THE BULKHEAD. KNOWING THE NOSE GEAR WAS NOT DOWN AND LOCKED, THE PILOT MADE AN EXCELLENT EMERGENCY LANDING CATCHING BOTH PROPS ON THE RUNWAY, BUT INCURRING ONLY MINOR DAMAGE TO THE AIRFRAME.

THE COVER WAS CONTACTING AND RUBBING AGAINST THE TAIL ROTOR DRIVE SHAFT. THE AFT PORTION OF THE COVER WAS PUSHED OVER TO THE RIGHT HAND ENGINE SIDE. A RIP IN THE COWLING WAS NOTICED ON THE LEFT HAND SIDE OF THE DRIVE SHAFT COVER BETWEEN THE 3RD AND 4TH DZUS FASTENER HOLES. HEAT DISCOLORATION ON THE COWLING WAS OBSERVED IN THAT SAME LOCATION. INSPECTORS OBSERVED THAT NONE OF THE 10 DZUS FASTENERS THAT SECURE THE DRIVE SHAFT COVER WERE ATTACHED TO THE LOWER SUPPORT STRUCTURE OF THE DRIVE SHAFT TUNNEL. INSPECTORS NOTICED LARGE AMOUNTS OF ALUMINUM DUST COVERING BOTH ENGINES AND IN THE ENGINE COMPARTMENT AREA. THE TAIL ROTOR DRIVE SHAFT SHOWED SIGNS OF HEAVY SCORING FROM RUBBING WITH THE STAINLESS STEEL DRIVE SHAFT COWLING. WHEN THE INSPECTORS REMOVED THE DRIVE SHAFT COWLING FROM THE DRIVE SHAFT, A 1/8 CUT COMPLETELY THROUGH THE DRIVE SHAFT WAS FOUND. INSPECTORS ROTATED THE TAIL ROTOR BLADE ASSEMBLY AND FOUND THAT DRIVE SHAFT FORWARD OF THE CUT DID NOT ROTATE. THE INSPECTORS PHOTOGRAPHED THE ENTIRE PROCESS FROM THE TIME THE ENGINE COWLING WAS OPEN TO THE TIME THE COVER WAS REMOVED FROM THE DRIVE SHAFT. INSPECTORS FOUND ONE OF THE DZUS FASTENERS LYING IN THE RIGHT HAND ENGINE AREA DECK DRAIN. THE FASTENER SHOWS SIGNS OF RUBBING AND WEAR MARKS ON THE COLLAR. THE CUT ON THE TAIL ROTOR DRIVE SHAFT MATCHED UP WITH A RIVET THAT HELD THE LEFT HAND, NUMBER ONE SPRING FOR THE DZUS FASTENER IN PLACE. THE RIVET, INSIDE THE COWLING SHOWS AN EXTREME AMOUNT OF RUBBING ON IT WITH HEAT DISCOLORING ON THE INSIDE OF THE DRIVE SHAFT COWLING.

PRIOR TO TOUCHDOWN, A SAFE LANDING WAS NEVER SERIOUSLY IN DOUBT AND I DID NOT FEEL IT NECESSARY TO ASSIST ON THE CONTROLS. I DO NOT FEEL THAT THE TOUCHDOWN WAS FIRM ENOUGH THAT IT SHOULD HAVE CAUSED ANY DAMAGE. LANDING GEAR FAILURE AT THE SHOCK STRUT ATTACHMENT POINTS HAS OCCURRED PREVIOUSLY IN THIS GLIDER AND MAY INDICATE A NEED FOR MORE FREQUENT INSPECTIONS OR A CHANGE IN THE COMPONENTS.

THE ACCIDENT SITE LACKED THE ODOR OF FUEL THAT MIGHT BE EXPECTED DUE TO THE RIGHT WING HAVING BEEN ALMOST SEVERED. TO PREVENT THE POSSIBLE LOSS OF REMAINING FUEL, THE LEFT AND RIGHT FUEL SELECTORS WERE CLOSED. THE LEFT WING FUEL CAP WAS REMOVED TO FACILITATE A VISUAL INSPECTION OF THE LEFT WING FUEL TANK. THE FUEL TANK WAS OBSERVED TO BE DRY. AN ATTEMPT WAS MADE TO SUMP THE LEFT WING TANK WITH NO FUEL NOTED. THE DIRECTOR OF MAINTENANCE FROM SKY LIMO CORPORATION HAD DRAINED THE REMAINING FUEL FROM THE RIGHT WING. LESS THAN A GALLON OF FUEL WAS RETRIEVED. THE COCKPIT FUEL INDICATOR WAS NOTED AS READING ZERO. THE FLAPS WERE ALSO NOTED AS BEING IN THE FULL-RETRACTED POSITION. A VISUAL INSPECTION OF THE FLAP CONTROL AND INDICATOR INSIDE THE COCKPIT CONFIRMED THIS CONDITION. AN INSPECTION OF BOTH ENGINES WAS CONDUCTED TO CHECK FOR PRESENCE OF FUEL. THE FUEL LINES TO THE LEFT AND RIGHT ENGINE SPIDERS WERE REMOVED. TRACE AMOUNTS OF FUEL WERE NOTED IN THE RIGHT SPIDER AND NO FUEL WAS DETECTED IN THE LEFT SPIDER. NO FUEL WAS DETECTED AT EITHER LEFT OR RIGHT FUEL INLET LINES AT ENGINE DRIVEN FUEL PUMPS. NO FUEL WAS DETECTED IN THE OUTLET SIDE OF THE LEFT ENGINE DRIVEN FUEL PUMP. A SMALL AMOUNT OF FUEL WAS FOUND IN THE OUTLET SIDE OF THE RIGHT ENGINE DRIVEN FUEL PUMP.

NO OTHER AIRCRAFT HAD ANY PROBLEMS WITH WATER CONTAMINATION. THE SOURCE OF THE FUEL WAS DETERMINED TO BE NOT CONTAMINATED. FBO PERSONNEL STATED THAT THE AIRCRAFT HAD ARRIVED AT KLNA ON 9 MAY. DURING THIS TIME, THERE HAD BEEN A SIGNIFICANT AMOUNT OF RAINFALL. THE POOR CONDITION OF THE LEFT WING FUEL CAP WHILE PARKED ON THE RAMP DURING THE PREVIOUS DAY'S RAINSTORMS COULD BE THE SOURCE OF THE WATER CONTAMINATION. IT WAS DETERMINED THE SIGNIFICANT AMOUNT OF WATER FOUND IN THE LEFT FUEL TANK AND ENGINE CARBURETOR WOULD HAVE CAUSED THE ENGINE TO CEASE OPERATING.

PROPELLER FINDINGS WERE AS FOLLOWS: PROP GOVERNOR - CABLE CONTINUITY AND OPERATION STOP TO STOP VERIFIFED. ONE PROP BLADE HAD BEEN BROKEN UPON IMPACT, PROP HUB WAS ALSO DAMAGED AT IMPACT. WHEN MORE FACTS BECOME KNOWN REGARDING THIS CASE, AN AMENDED REPORT WILL BE FILED. (-23 AMENDMENT) NEITHER THE FAA NOR THE NTSB KNOWS FOR SURE WHAT CAUSED THIS ACCIDENT. HOWEVER, IT APPEARS THAT THERE WAS A MISSING BOLT FROM THE LEFT ELEVATOR BOW THAT WAS SHEARED/TWISTED AND FAILED WHICH MEANS THAT THE LEFT ELEVATOR WAS FREE FROM THE CONTROL SYSTEM AND, THEREFORE, UNCONTROLLABLE BY THE PILOT. THIS WOULD HAVE CAUSED AN INVERSE YAW CONDITION WHICH THE PILOT WOULD HAVE ATTEMPTED TO COUNTERACT WITH LEFT RUDDER AND AILERON. THIS WOULD HAVE CAUSED DRAG AND LOSS OF ALTITUDE WHICH THE PILOT WOULD HAVE ATTEMPTED TO OVERCOME WITH MORE ENGINE POWER. SINCE THE ENGINE WAS ABOVE THE LONGITUDINAL AXIS, MORE ENGINE POWER WOULD HAVE LED TO THE AIRCRAFT NOSING DOWNWARD. THE AIRCRAFT DID STRIKE THE GROUND NOSE FIRST. THE PILOT STILL HAS NO MEMORY OF THE ACCIDENT. THIS IS A FINAL REPORT UNLESS FURTHER INFORMATION BECOMES KNOWN.

THESE WINDS WERE WELL WITHIN THE LIMITS OF THE B-1900D FOR RUNWAY 12R AND THE GIVEN AIRCRAFT CONFIGURATION AND WEIGHT, AND TEMPERATURE. THE SKY CONDITIONS WERE CLEAR AND THE VISIBILITY WAS 10+ SM. THE SIC STATES THAT AT APPROXIMATELY TWO MILES OUT ON FINAL APPROACH THE AIRCRAFT WAS SLIGHTLY HIGH AND AT VREF +15 KIAS. THE PIC WAS THE FLYING PILOT. THE SIC CALLED THIS DEVIATION OUT TO THE PIC AND THE PIC ACKNOWLEDGED, BUT THE PIC NEVER CORRECTED THE DEVIATION. AT SOME POINT BETWEEN SHORT-FINAL AND PASSING OVER THE THRESHOLD, THE PIC LOWERED THE NOSE SLIGHTLY TO GET BACK ON GLIDESLOPE, THUS MOST LIKELY INCREASING THE AIRSPEED SOMEWHAT. BOTH THE PIC AND SIC STATE THAT THE AIRCRAFT CROSSED THE THRESHOLD AT VREF +10. THE AIRCRAFT FLOATED, OR RATHER WAS ALLOWED TO FLOAT A CONSIDERABLE DISTANCE DOWN THE 5000' RUNWAY, APPROXIMATELY 1/2+ THE AVAILABLE RUNWAY LENGTH, TOUCHING DOWN APPROXIMATELY 2900 FEET FROM THE RWY APPROACH END AT TAXIWAY "H"; THIS WAS VERIFIED BY BOTH THE PIC AND SIC, AND TWO KVGT AIRPORT EMPLOYEES WHO WITNESSED THE LANDING. AT THIS POINT, THE REMAINING STOPPING DISTANCE AVAILABLE WAS APPROXIMATELY 2100 FEET. THE SIC STATES THAT AS THE AIRCRAFT FLOATED DOWN THE RUNWAY THAT HE ADVISED THE PIC THAT HE (PIC) WAS LONG, I.E., LANDING LONG. THE PIC ACKNOWLEDGED AND CONTINUED TO LAND THE AIRCRAFT. THE SIC DID NOT ADVISE THE PIC THAT A GO-AROUND SHOULD BE INITIATED AND THE PIC DID NOT INITIATE A GO-AROUND. UPON TOUCHDOWN, THE PIC IMMEDIATELY APPLIED MAXIMUM REVERSE THRUST AND BRAKING. AT A POINT APPROXIMATELY 300 FEET FROM THE END OF THE RUNWAY, THE PIC ASKED FOR THE SIC TO HELP WITH THE BRAKING; THE SIC THEN ALSO APPLIED MAXIMUM BRAKING. THE AIRCRAFT IS NOT EQUIPPED WITH AN ANTI-SKID SYSTEM, THUS ALL FOUR MAIN WHEELS LOCKED UP AT SOME POINT. THE AIRCRAFT THEN BEGAN TO VEER OFF TO THE LEFT SLIGHTLY, EVENTUALLY STRAIGHTENING OUT, AND CONTINUING TO SLOW DOWN. THE AIRCRAFT EXITED THE END OF THE RUNWAY, ON THE LEFT SIDE, AND STOPPING APPROXIMATELY AN AIRCRAFT'S LENGTH ON THE HARD SURFACE OF THE OVERRUN AREA. AS THE AIRCRAFT PASSED THE END OF THE RUNWAY, THE LEFT PROPELLER AND LEFT MAIN GEAR CAME IN CONTACT WITH A RUNWAY-END IDENTIFIER LIGHT. THE LIGHT WAS DESTROYED AND TWO OF THE FOUR PROPELLER BLADES WERE DAMAGED. DURING THE MAXIMUM BRAKING, 3 OF THE 4 MAIN TIRES WERE FLAT-SPOTTED. THE LIGHT, PROPELLER, AND TIRES ALL NEEDED TO BE REPLACED. THE PIC THEN CONTINUED TO TAXI TO THE RAMP AND DEPLANE THE PASSENGERS. THE CREW HAD NOTICED THE FLAT-SPOTTED TIRES WHILE TAXIING TO THE RAMP AREA AND THE DAMAGE TO THE PROPELLER DURING THE POST-FLIGHT WALK-AROUND. THE PIC ENTERED THE MECHANICAL DISCREPANCIES IN THE AIRCRAFT LOGBOOK PER NORMAL COMPANY PROCEDURES, ADVISED THE DISPATCHER OF THE INCIDENT, AND THE PIC AND SIC SUBMITTED COMPANY AVIATION SAFETY REPORTS (ASRS). INSPECTOR EXAMINED THE PRIMARY AND STANDBY ALTERNATOR FOR ANY OBVIOUS DISCREPANCIES. UPON COMPLETION, IT WAS NOTED ON THE PRIMARY ALTERNATOR THAT THE AUX LUG WAS LOOSE (AUX LUG SUPPLIES POWER TO THE ANNUNCIATOR PANEL). INSPECTOR THEN REQUESTED THAT MECHANIC REMOVE THE TOP COVER OF THE BATTERY BOX TO INSPECT THE INTEGRITY OF THE BATTERY AND TERMINAL CONNECTIONS. UPON REMOVAL OF THE COVER, INSPECTOR FOUND THE GROUND CABLE (NEG) SEVERELY CORRODED IN AND AROUND TERMINAL LUG. IN ADDITION, INSPECTOR EXAMINED EMERGENCY LANDING GEAR PROCEDURES "QUICK REFERENCE" CARD. EMERGENCY LANDING GEAR PROCEDURE REQUIRES THAT THE PIC PULL THE LANDING GEAR CIRCUIT BREAKER (30 AMP) AND CRANK DOWN THE GEAR BETWEEN 45 AND 50 TURNS. INSPECTOR REQUESTED THAT MECHANIC DUPLICATE PROCEDURE TO DEMONSTRATE THE INTEGRITY OF THE MANUAL EXTENSION OF THE LANDING GEAR. IN DOING SO, MECHANIC WAS UNABLE TO PULL OUT THE 30 AMP C/B, AS WELL AS THE INSPECTOR. DISCREPANCY WAS NOTED AND COMMUNICATED TO OWNER. ON 12/14/2006, A REVIEW OF THE AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE LOG BOOKS WAS COMPLETED. IT APPEARS THAT THE PRIMARY ALTERNATOR HAS BEEN REPLACED IN 3/2005, AND 3/2006, WITH NO REASON OR EXPLANATION AS TO WHY THERE WERE YEARLY FAILURES WITH THE ALTERNATOR. THIS CASE IS CONSIDERED CLOSED.

ON TUESDAY MORNING 1/9/2007 THE NTSB, A PIPER AIRCRAFT ACCIDENT INVESTIGATOR, AND A LYCOMING ENGINE INVESTIGATOR WERE ON SCENE. WE WENT BACK OUT TO THE CRASH SITE TO CONTINUE WITH THE INVESTIGATION. ALL PARTIES TOOK MORE PICTURES AND DOCUMENTED THE AREA INCLUDING THE DEBRIS FIELD SIZE AND DIRECTION. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE WRECKAGE NEEDED TO BE MOVED OUT OF THE ELEMENTS AS THE AREA WAS A MARSH WITH TWO TO FOUR INCHES OF STANDING WATER AND MORE SNOW WAS FORECASTED. THE NTSB INVESTIGATOR ARRANGED FOR A LOCAL CONTRACTOR, WHO WAS WORKING ON THE AIRPORT, TO MOVE THE WRECKAGE TO A HANGAR THAT WAS VOLUNTEERED BY A LOCAL AIRCRAFT OWNER. ON TUESDAY AFTERNOON THE WRECKAGE WAS MOVED TO THIS HANGAR AND THE HANGAR WAS SECURED FOR THE NIGHT. ON WEDNESDAY 1/10/2007, ALL THE PARTIES INVOLVED MET AT THE HANGAR AND STARTED TO INVENTORY THE WRECKAGE. BOTH ENGINES WERE BROKEN OFF THEIR MOUNTS FROM THE FIREWALL DURING THE IMPACT. THE ENGINES WERE EXAMINED AND THE ACCESSORIES WERE REMOVED INCLUDING THE PROPELLERS TO VERIFY ROTATION. BOTH ENGINES WERE ABLE TO BE ROTATED AND HAD FUEL PRESENT TO THE FUEL INJECTORS. THE SPARK PLUGS WERE EXAMINED AND FOUND TO BE SERVICEABLE. THE OIL SCREENS WERE INSPECTED AND LEFT ENGINE WAS NORMAL WHILE THE RIGHT ENGINE SHOWED SIGNS OF BEARING MATERIAL. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE AMOUNT OF BEARING WEAR DID NOT AFFECT THE PERFORMANCE OF THE ENGINE THIS DAY. BOTH ENGINE THROTTLE PLATES WERE FOUND IN THE CLOSED (IDLE) POSITION. THE IGNITION SYSTEMS OF BOTH ENGINES WERE FOUND TO BE FUNCTIONING EXCEPT THAT THE LEFT ENGINE RIGHT MAGNETO HAD BROKEN OFF OF THE ENGINE ON IMPACT AND COULD NOT BE LOCATED AS OF THIS DATE. THE AIRFRAME EXAMINATION REVEALED THAT THE ENGINE CONTROL QUADRANT HAD THE MIXTURES SELECTED IN THE FULL RICH POSITION, THE PROPELLER LEVERS FULL FORWARD IN LOW PITCH, AND THE THROTTLES WERE IN THE IDLE POSITION WHICH IS CONFIRMED BY THE ENGINE THROTTLE PLATES BEING IN THE CLOSED POSITION. THE FUEL SYSTEM CONTROL VALVES WERE LOCATED AND FOUND TO BE DAMAGED BUT THE VALVE POSITION COULD BE VERIFIED. THE PIPER INVESTIGATOR STATED THE VALVE POSITIONS AS FOLLOWS: RIGHT FUEL SYSTEM CROSS FEED VALVE OPEN, SHUT OFF VALVE CLOSED AND THE LEFT FUEL SYSTEM CROSS FEED VALVE OPEN AND SHUT OFF VALVE OPEN. THE FLIGHT CONTROLS WERE LOCATED AND CONTINUITY AS FAR AS THE PUSH PULL TUBES AND BELLCRANKS ARE CONCERNED WAS CONFIRMED. THE LANDING GEAR WAS RETRACTED AS WERE THE FLAPS AT THE TIME OF IMPACT.

PILOT STATEMENT: AFTER TAKE-OFF, ENGINES DID NOT SOUND RIGHT, NOTIFIED TOWER AND REQUESTED RETURN TO AIRPORT. SWITCHED THE FUEL TANKS, ENGINES STILL DID NOT SOUND RIGHT. LANDED WITH FLAPS OUT AND GEAR GREEN LIGHT. TOUCHED DOWN AND THE NOSE AND RIGHT MAIN GEAR COLLAPSED. AIRPORT MANAGER STATEMENT AT THE SCENE STATED: PROPELLER STRIKES IN THE RUNWAY SHOW THAT BOTH PROPELLERS CONTACTED THE RUNWAY AT THE SAME TIME. BOTH PROPELLERS WERE BENT AROUND THE COWLING INDICATING THAT THE ENGINES WERE AT HIGH POWER UPON LANDING. INSPECTOR STATEMENT FEBRUARY 6, 2007: TOGETHER WITH INSPECTORS ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ , I ^PRIVACY DATA OMIT^ ASSISTED IN PERFORMING AN INCIDENT INVESTIGATION ON N694T AT PADUCAH AIRPORT (KPAH), KENTUCKY, ON FEBRUARY 5, 2007                           . AN INSPECTION OF THE MAIN AUXILIARY FUEL TANK FOR WATER CONTAMINATION WAS PERFORMED, THE FOLLOWING WAS OBSERVED: THE AIRCRAFT'S LEFT AND RIGHT MAIN FUEL TANKS SHOWED NO EVIDENCE OF WATER CONTAMINATION. AN ATTEMPT TO GET A SAMPLE FROM THE LEFT AUXILIARY FUEL TANK INDICATED THAT THE TANK WAS EMPTY. A SAMPLE OF THE RIGHT AUXILIARY FUEL TANK WAS NOT POSSIBLE DUE TO A STUCK SUMP DRAIN. AN ATTEMPT TO UNFREEZE THE DRAIN WAS MADE BY A MECHANIC FROM MIDWEST AVIATION AND WAS UNSUCCESSFUL. POWER WAS SUPPLIED TO THE AIRCRAFT TO GET AN INDICATION OF THE FUEL QUANTITY GAUGES. THE FUEL QUANTITY GAUGES INDICATED THAT THE LEFT AND RIGHT MAIN FUEL TANKS WERE EMPTY AND THE AUXILIARY LEFT AND RIGHT TANKS SHOWED HALF FULL. I ASKED THE PILOT IF HE SUMPED ALL TANKS PRIOR TO SATURDAY'S FLIGHT, HE STATED THAT HE ALWAYS CHECKS THE MAIN TANKS, WHEN ASKED ABOUT THE AUXILIARY TANKS HE DID NOT RESPOND WITH AN ANSWER. THE PILOT STATED THAT THE ENGINES WERE RUNNING FINE ON LANDING. ANALYSIS: THE PILOT ^PRIVACY DATA OM^ THE PILOT OF N694T DID NOT COMPLETE A PROPER PREFLIGHT WHEN HE NEGLECTED TO SUMP ALL THE FUEL TANKS. THE PILOT ^PRIVACY DA^ ALSO DEPARTED THE AIRPORT WITH A MINIMUM AMOUNT OF FUEL IN THE MAIN FUEL TANKS. (THE FLIGHT LASTED APPROXIMATELY FIVE MINUTES, THE FUEL INDICATION AFTER THE CRASH MAINS EMPTY, AUX TANKS ONE HALF FULL). THE PILOT ^PRIVACY DATA OM^ STATED THAT THE ENGINES DID NOT SOUND RIGHT. THE AIRCRAFT HAD BEEN PARKED OUTSIDE IN FRIGID TEMPERATURES, THERE IS THE POSSIBILITY THAT THE ENGINE OIL TEMPERATURE WERE NOT UP TO OPERATING TEMPERATURE. THIS COULD HAVE PREVENTED THE PROPELLERS FROM GOING TO FINE PITCH WHICH WOULD GIVE A DIFFERENT SOUND THAN FINE PITCH AT FULL POWER. THIS WOULD ALSO ACCOUNT WHY THE ENGINES SOUNDED OK ON LANDING AFTER THE OIL TEMPERATURE REACHED THE NORMAL OPERATING RANGE. ON LANDING, BOTH PROPELLERS CONTACTED THE RUNWAY AT THE SAME TIME. THIS INDICATES THAT A NOSE DOWN LANDING WAS ATTEMPTED OR THE NOSE GEAR COLLAPSED. BOTH PROPELLERS WERE SEVERELY BENT INDICATING THAT THE ENGINES WERE TURNING AT HIGH POWER. CONCLUSION: ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ .

MARKS IN THE SAND AT THIS POINT, AND DAMAGE TO THE PROPELLER ARE CONSISTENT WITH AN ENGINE PRODUCING GREATER THAN IDLE POWER. THE PROPELLER AND NOSE GEAR CAME TO REST APPROXIMATELY 150 FEET AND 170 FEET RESPECTIVELY FROM THE THRESHOLD EDGE, ON THE SAME ENERGY LINE APPROXIMATELY 75 DEGREES TO THE RUNWAY CENTERLINE. THE OUTBOARD 60 PERCENT OF THE RIGHT WING LEADING EDGE WAS CRUSHED AND THE ENTIRE WING PANEL DEFLECTED UP 15 DEGREES AT THE POINT WHERE THE STRUT ATTACHED TO THE SPAR. THE INBOARD END OF THE RIGHT AILERON WAS DEFORMED. THE DORSAL AND SIDE SKINS OF THE AFT FUSELAGE WERE DEFORMED SHOWING EVIDENCE OF SIGNIFICANT TORSION LOADS, LIKELY THE RESULT OF THE IMPACT ON THE NOSE. THE PROPELLER AND SPINNER HAD SEPARATED FROM THE ENGINE AS A UNIT. THE PROPELLER BLADES WERE SCORED AND CURLED AFT. THE NOSE LANDING GEAR STRUT HAD SEPARATED AT THE MOUNTING TRUNNION. MOST OF THE NOSE GEAR FAIRING WAS STILL ATTACHED AND INTACT. THE COCKPIT, COCKPIT FLOOR AND INSTRUMENT PANEL WERE DEFORMED, HAVING PULLED AWAY FROM THE AIRFRAME WITH THE FIREWALL AND ENGINE. THE WINDSHIELD WAS DESTROYED. THE LEFT MAIN TIRE/WHEEL ASSEMBLY WAS BENT OUTWARD 30 DEGREES WHERE IT ATTACHED TO THE SPRING STEEL STRUT. CONTROLS: INVESTIGATORS WERE UNABLE TO ESTABLISH CONTROL CONTINUITY TO ANY CONTROL SURFACE DUE TO THE DESTRUCTION OF THE PRIMARY CONTROL CONNECTIONS AT THE FIREWALL. IN THE COCKPIT THE FOLLOWING POSITIONS AND INDICATIONS WERE NOTED: FUEL SELECTOR - BOTH, PROPS - FULL FWD, PRIMER - IN/LOCKED, COWL FLAPS - CLOSED, MIXTURE - RICH, CARB HEAT - OFF, FLAPS - 10 DEGREES, PARKING BRAKE - OFF, THROTTLE - LOW POWER, MAGNETOS - BOTH, ALTIMETER - 2460' (29.92). THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF FUEL STARVATION, FUEL EXHAUSTION, OR ENGINE FAILURE. THE PHYSICAL EVIDENCE, TOGETHER WITH PILOT AND WITNESS STATEMENTS LEADS TO LOSS OF CONTROL AS THE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT. WITH FULL POWER APPLIED AND AIRSPEED INDICATING 40-45 KNOTS, THE PILOT ^PRIVA^ REALIZED HE WOULD BE UNABLE TO CLIMB. HE CHOSE A VACANT LOT STRAIGHT AHEAD FOR A LANDING. DAMAGE: THE FLAPS APPEARED TO BE FULLY EXTENDED AND UNDAMAGED. THE LEFT WING STRUT HAD FAILED AT THE MIDDLE, POSSIBLY THE RESULT OF TORSION LOADS ON THE FUSELAGE. THE CABIN WAS INTACT. THE PROPELLER HAD SUFFERED SIGNIFICANT DAMAGE AND WAS DEFLECTED AFT FROM CONTACTING THE BERM UNDER POWER. THE FRONT AND BOTTOM OF THE ENGINE COWLING WAS CRUSHED. THE AFT FUSELAGE STRUCTURE HAD FAILED AND DEFORMED DUE TO THE VERTICAL STABILIZER CONTACTING THE GROUND. THE DORSAL EXTREMITIES OF THE VERTICAL STABILIZER AND RUDDER WERE CRUSHED DOWN 4-6 INCHES. THE SINK TURNED INTO MORE LAMINAR AIR ABOUT 1/8 MILE FROM THE RUNWAY AND I TRADED MY EXTRA SPEED FOR ALTITUDE I HAD ALREADY DECIDED TO GIVE UP ON TRYING TO THERMAL OUT OF HERE IN THIS TRASHY AIR. I CAN CALL FOR THE TOW PLANE TO COME GET ME OR I CAN CALL FOR MY TRAILER AND TAKE IT APART AND DRIVE HOME. IN THAT LAST 1/8 MILE OF RELATIVE CALM I HAD A GOOD CHANCE TO LOOK OVER THE AIRPORT FOR MY LANDING. I GOT BACK OVER THE 34 NUMBERS AT 400 FEET AGL AND HAD THE OPTION OF TURNING FINAL FROM THERE AND LANDING LONG AND PUSHING THE GLIDER BACK 4000 FEET ON THE TAXIWAY OR TURNING WHAT NEEDED TO BE A 450 DEGREE LEFT TURN TO GET MORE LOGICAL SPACING ON THE RUNWAY. MY GLIDER WILL DO A 360 DEGREE TURN WITH A LOSS OF LESS THAN 100' WHICH WOULD PUT ME ABOUT RIGHT FOR A SHORT BASE TO FINAL. ACCORDING TO THE TRACE THAT SAMPLES EVERY 4 SECONDS, THE FIRST 120 DEGREES OF THE TURN WAS BENIGN FOR LIFT OR SINK. THE REST OF THE TURN UNTIL IMPACT WAS IN 600 FPM SINK. THIS TWIN-ENGINE TURBINE POWERED HELICOPTER'S MAXIMUM GROSS WEIGHT IS 38,000 POUNDS, AND IT WAS BEING OPERATED UNDER AN "ON CALL" CONTRACT FOR THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA (CALFIRE) IN SUPPORT OF WILD LAND FIRE SUPPRESSION ACTIVITIES ON THE ZACA FIRE INCIDENT LOCATED IN SANTA BARBARA COUNTY. DURING THE ON-SCENE INVESTIGATION, PHYSICAL EVIDENCE CONSISTING OF A NUT, BOLT, AND PLATE WAS FOUND APPROXIMATELY SIX FEET FROM THE WRECKAGE. THIS PIN ASSEMBLY SECURES ONE OF THREE SERVO UNITS TO THE HELICOPTER TRANSMISSION ON ONE END AND THE HELICOPTER SWASH PLATE ON THE OTHER END. ATTACHED TO THE PIN VIA A BOLT, IS A PIN LOCKING HOLDER WITH A RECEIVING HOLE ON THE OPPOSITE END. THIS PIN IS PLACED THROUGH AN OUTSIDE ATTACH LUG WHICH IS INTEGRAL TO THE TRANSMISSION CASE, THEN THROUGH LOWER SERVO ATTACH LUG AND INTO AN INSIDE ATTACH LUG (AGAIN INTEGRAL TO THE TRANSMISSION CASE), WHICH SECURES THE COLLECTIVE SERVO (CONTROL DEVICE) TO THE SWASH PLATE. THIS GIVES THE PILOT DIRECTIONAL CONTROL TO THE MAIN ROTOR. THE PIN LOCKING HOLDER ATTACHED TO THE OUTSIDE END OF THE PIN IS A SAFETY RETENTION DEVICE WHICH SLIDES OVER A STUD ON THE HELICOPTER'S TRANSMISSION CASE. THERE IS A NUT THAT IS FASTENED ONTO THE STUD THEN SAFETY-WIRED TO THE BOLT WHICH ATTACHES THE PIN LOCKING HOLDER TO THE PIN. THIS ENTIRE ASSEMBLY WAS LOCATED SEVERAL YARDS AWAY FROM THE MAIN WRECKAGE. FURTHER INVESTIGATION OF THE TRANSMISSION CASE PIN RETENTION STUD WHICH RETAINS AND SECURES THE PIN THAT ATTACHES THE COLLECTIVE SERVO TO THE TRANSISSION CASE HAS EXCESSIVE WERAR FROM FRETTING AT THE LOWER 3/16 INCH OF THE STUD FROM BEARING CONTACT FROM THE PIN RETENTION STRAP. THE THREADS IN THE AREA OF THE RETAINING NUT CONTACT (CENTER AND UPPER PORTION OF THE STUD) HAD DEFORMED THREADS THAT WERE  DEFORMED UPWARD (OR AWAY FROM THE TRANSMISSION CASE). THE THREAD DEFORMATION APPEARS TO HAVE BEEN THE RESULT OF TENSION/COMPRESSIVE OVERLOAD DUE TO PN AND STRAP SEPARATION. THE 14 INCH X 28 RETAINING NUT HAD SEPARATED FROM THE STUD AND WAS ATTACHED TO THE PIN RETENTION BOLT BY SAFETY WIRE. THE THREADS ON THE NUT APPEARED TO BE DEFORMED FROM WEAR AND OVERLOAD. THE INSIDE ATTACH LUG, INTEGRAL TO THE TRANSMISSION CASE, HAS A CLOSED END BUSHING INSTALLED WHICH PROVIDES A BEARING SURFACE FOR THE PIN AND ALSO PREVENTS MAIN TRANSMISSION LUBRICATION OIL FROM LEAKING OUT OF THE CASE. THIS BUSHING IS MANUFACTURED WITH A FLAT END SURFACE PERPENDICULAR TO THE ROUND BUSHING OD. THE INSTALLED BUSHING APPEARED DEFORMED FROM CONTACT OF AN INTERIOR TRANSMISSION PART OR COMPONENT. IT IS NOT KNOWN WHAT FORCE IS REQURIED, DURING HELICOPTER OPERATION, TO "PUSH" THE PIN AND STRAP ASSEMBLY OUT OF THE BUSHINGS BORES. THE FORCE HOWEVER TO ROLLOVER AND DEFORM THE THREADS ON THE STUD WOULD BE MORE THAN NORMAL VIBRATION FORCES AND WOULD HAVE REQUIRED AN EXTERNAL/INTERNAL FORCE TO CAUSE THE RETAINING NUT TO BE PULLED OFF THE THREADS. THE STUD THREAD SIGNATURES SUBSTANTIATE THE APPLICATION OF AN INTERNAL FORCE THAT PUSHED THE PIN OUT OF ITS INSTALLED POSITION. THE APPLIED FORCE WAS STRONG ENOUGH TO PUSH THE PIN OUT OF THE BUSHING BORES AND TO CAUSE THE RETAINING PLATE TO DEPART THE STUD AND PUSH THE THREADED NUT OFF THE STUD. THE NUT, PIN, RETENTION STRAP AND STUD ARE FLIGHT SAFETY CRITICAL COMPONENTS. HOWEVER, IF THE INSIDE BUSHING, MANUFACTURED BY HEAVY LIFT HELICOPTERS, INC IS NOT MANUFACTURED TO CORRECT TOLERANCES AND AS WEAR TAKES PLACE INSIDE THE MAIN TRANSMISSION AND TOLERANCES CHANGE, INTERNAL MECHANICAL FORCES COULD "PUSH" THIS PIN ASSEMBLY AND NUT OFF OF THE STUD. THIS WILL CAUSE THE SEPARATION OF THE SERVO UNIT, AND CONSEQUENTLY CAUSE MAIN ROTOR BLADE PITCH CONTROL LOSS. THE LOSS OF CONTROL WOULD LIKELY MANIFES

SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE RESULTED TO THE LEFT WING. THE BRAKE SYSTEM WAS WORKING BUT APPARENTLY THE MECHANIC RELEASED THE BRAKES AS HE WAS TRYING TO GAIN CONTROL OF THE AIRCRAFT. THE DETERMINATION OF CLASSIFYING THIS SITUATION AS IN INCIDENT WEAS MADE FROM THE FACT THAT THE AIRCRAFT OPERATION WAS BEING ACCOMPLISHED FOR MAINTENANCE PURPOSES AND WITHOUT THE INTENT TO OPERATE FOR AIR NAVIGATION. FURTHERMORE, AFTER INTERVIEWING THE MECHANIC IT WEAS DETERMINED THAT THERE WAS NO CARELESSNESS OR RECKLESS OF INTENT AND FAR 91.13(B) WAS NOT CITED IN THIS SITUATION.

APPARENTLY THE ROCKER ARM WAS IN THE PROCESS OF BACKING OFF THE CYLINDER AND HAD THE PROPER PROCEDURE BEEN USED TO INSTALL THE CYLINDER THE DISCREPANCY WOULD HAVE BEEN NOTED AND CORRECTED, PREVENTING THE ACCIDENT.

THE PILOT HAD A PRIVATE PILOT CERTIFICATE AND WAS RATED FOR AIRPLANE SINGLE ENGINE LAND AND INSTRUMENT. NO VIOLATIONS ON RECORD. THIS ACCIDENT REPORT IS CLOSED.

(-23 AMENDMENT) NOTE: THE POSSIBILITY THE PILOT FAILED IN HIS ATTEMPT TO SECURE THE BAGGAGE DOOR CORRECTLY IS OBVIOUS. HOWEVER THE QUESTION IS, "WERE THERE EXTENUATING CIRCUMSTANCES THAT CONTRIBUTED TO THIS FAILURE, WHEN SECURING THIE PARTICULAR TYPE BAGGAGE DOOR?" SEE ITEM #4, FAA NINE RESPONSIBILITIES.  CONCLUSION: THE PILOT APPARENTLY FAILED TO PROPERLY SECURE THE FORWARD BAGGAGE DOOR, WHICH ALLOWED IT TO OPEN DURING TAKEOFF.  ACCORDING TO 14 CFR 91.3 (A) THE PILOT IN COMMAND IS DIRECTLY RESPONSIBLE FOR, AND IS THE FINAL AUTHORITY AS TO, THE OPERATION OF THAT AIRCRAFT.  DURING THE COURSE OF THIS INVESTIGATION NUMEROUS ANOMALIES WERE UNCOVERED AND CORRECTIVE RECOMMENDATIONS ARE CURRENTLY BEING CONSIDER BY THE FAA AND THE MANUFACTURE.

20080301832719I	(-23) NWA FLIGHT #1749 DEPARTED KMSP ENROUTE TO MMCZ. SHORTLY AFTER LEVEL OFF THE FIRST OFFICER NOTICED A FUEL IMBALANCE GREATER THAN THAT ALLOWABLE. THE AMOUNT OF FUEL USED (TOTAL FUEL LOADED MINUS FUEL ONBOARD) AND THE FUEL BURN NUMBERS WERE CORRECT, HOWEVER IT APPEARED ALL OF THE FUEL, FOR BOTH ENGINES WAS BEING BURNED OUT OF THE RIGHT MAIN FUEL TANK. AFTER DISCUSSION WITH DISPATCH AND MTC, THE DECISION WAS MADE TO DIVERT TO KMEM. IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE FUELER IN KMSP HAD LEFT THE MODE SELECT SWITCH ON THE REFUELING CONTROL PANEL IN THE REFUEL POSITION AND THE REFUELING VALVE FOR THE LEFT WING IN THE OPEN POSITION. ALSO, A RELAY, REMOVED AFTER THE EVENT, WAS DETERMINED TO HAVE FAILED IN SUCH A MANNER THAT NO ELECTRICAL POWER WAS AVAILABLE TO CLOSE THE TWO OPEN FUELING VALVES WHEN THE LANDING GEAR SELECTOR WAS RAISED. THE FAILED RELAY PREVENTED THE FLOW OF POWER TO THE SHUT SECTION OF THE TWO VALVES INVOLVED. THUS THE FUEL BOOST PUMP PRESSURE MOVED THE FUEL FROM THE CENTER/RIGHT WING TANK TO THE LEFT WING TANK.

INVESTIGATION OF THE WRECKAGE SHOWED THE ATTACH POINTS FOR THE TAIL SECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT HAD SEPARATED FROM THE FUSELAGE.  THE STUBS THAT FIT INTO THE SOCKETS THAT HOLD THE TAIL ON HAVE STUBS THAT BOLTS SHOULD GO THROUGH. THEY HAD NO HOLES THROUGH THEM. THE SOCKETS THAT THE STUBS FIT INTO SHOWED SIGNS OF WEAR.  THE AIRCRAFT HAD NO AIRWORTHINESS CERTIFICATE AND HAD NOT BEEN INSPECTED BY THE FAA OR ITS REPRESENTATIVE.  ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ WAS THE BUILDER OF THE AIRCRAFT WITH THE HELP OF ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^.  THE TAIL SECTION IS SECURED BY TWO ATTACH POINTS OF POST AND SOCKET STYLE DESIGN, I.E. A TUBULAR STUB IS SECURED IN A TUBULAR SOCKET THEN A THROUGH-BOLT IS INSERTED THROUGH BOTH PIECES AND SECURED WITH A BOLT AND SELF-LOCKING NUT.  THE BOLT HOLES ARE PREDRILLED IN THE SOCKET BUT NOT IN THE TUBULAR STUB WHICH MUST BE DRILLED BY THE AIRCRAFT ASSEMBLER.  FROM PAINT SIGNATURES ON THE STUBS AND WEAR PATTERNS IN THE SOCKETS, IT APPEARS AS IF THE STUBS WERE NOT INSERTED DEEP ENOUGH INTO THE SOCKETS TO BLOCK THE PREDRILLED BOLT HOLES.  HAD THE ASSEMBLER PROPERLY INSERTED THE UNDRILLED STUBS INTO THE SOCKETS HE WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN ABLE TO INSERT THE BOLTS THROUGH THE SOCKET STUB ASSEMBLY.  AS IT WAS, IT APPEARS THAT THE BOLT WAS INSERTED THROUGH THE SOCKET BELOW THE STUB THEREFORE PROHIBITING A POSITIVE LOCK. IT ALSO APPEARS AS THOUGH SOME PINCHING OF THE STUB MAY HAVE OCCURRED AS A RESULT OF TIGHTENING THE THROUGH-BOLT WHICH MAY HAVE PRESENTED THE FALSE INDICATION TO THE ASSEMBLER THAT THE CONNECTION WAS SECURE WHEN INDEED IT WAS NOT.

20080611843569I	(-23) DURING THE DESCENT TO THE DESTINATION AIRPORT AT APPROXIMATELY FL200 IN THE VICINITY OF EVERETT, WA, THE FLIGHT CREW AND OTHER AIRCRAFT OCCUPANTS HEARD AND FELT A DISTINCT THUMP.  THE CAPTAIN CHECKED ALL ENGINE INSTRUMENTS AND NOTED NO CHANGE OR ABNORMAL INDICATIONS.  A FLIGHT ATTENDANT CALLED THE FLIGHT DECK DUE TO PASSENGER INQUIRIES, BUT THE FLIGHT CREW COULD NOT PROVIDE AN ANSWER AS TO THE CAUSE.  ANOTHER FLIGHT ATTENDANT CALL WAS MADE LATER IN THE DESCENT TO INFORM THE CAPTAIN THAT A PASSENGER REPORTED HAVING SEEN SOMETHING THAT LOOKED LIKE A PANEL.  AFTER AN UNEVENTFUL LANDING IN BELLINGHAM, WA (BLI), AN INSPECTION REVEALED A LARGE DENT ON THE INBOARD LEADING EDGE OF THE RIGHT WING (ON THE SLAT).  THE DENT WAS APPROXIMATELY 8 INCHES ACROSS, 6 INCHES VERTICALLY, AND 2 INCHES DEEP.  THERE WAS NO BLOOD OR FEATHERS TO INDICATE A BIRD MIGHT HAVE BEEN THE CAUSE.  THERE WAS ALSO A SMALL DENT ON THE LEADING EDGE OF THE RIGHT ENGINE NOSE COWL.  THIS DENT COULD BE READILY SEEN FROM THE FRONT OF THE AIRCRAFT LOOKING REARWARD AND WAS AT THE 10 O'CLOCK POSITION.  THE AIRLINE FLEW A NEW SLAT SECTION TO BLI AND REPAIRED THE RIGHT WING DENT THAT NIGHT.  AIRLINE MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL AT BLI INSPECTED THE AIRPLANE AND VERIFIED THERE WERE NO MISSING PARTS OR DOORS THAT COULD HAVE CAUSED THE DAMAGE.  THEY ALSO INSPECTED THE RIGHT ENGINE TO VERIFY THAT NO FOD DAMAGE WAS PRESENT.  MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL ALSO REPLACED THE RIGHT ENGINE NOSE COWL AFTER FLYING REVENUE FLIGHTS FOR ONE DAY.  THE AIRLINE RECEIVED PERMISSION FROM BOEING ENGINEERING TO FLY WITH THE MINOR DENT FOR ONE DAY TO PROVIDE TIME TO TRANSPORT THE REPLACEMENT PART.  AN FAA OPERATIONS INSPECTOR ASSIGNED TO THE ALLEGIANT AIR CMT WAS ONBOARD IN THE COCKPIT DURING THIS INCIDENT AND WAS ASSIGNED AS THE FAA IIC FOR THIS INVESTIGATION.  THE POSSIBLILITY THAT THE OBJECT WAS A WEATHER BALLOON HAS BEEN CONSIDERED.  HOWEVER, WEATHER BALLOONS ARE LAUNCHED ON A STANDARD SCHEDULE THAT DOES NOT CORRELATE WITH THE TIME OF THIS FLIGHT.  THEREFORE, IT IS VERY UNLIKELY THIS WAS A BALLOON LAUNCHED BY THE NATIONAL WEATHER SERVICE.  RADAR DATA FROM THE SEATTLE AIR ROUTE TRAFFIC CONTROL CENTER INDICATES THERE WERE NO OTHER AIRCRAFT AT A HIGHER ALTITUDE AND IN A POSITION FROM WHICH A PART MAY HAVE FALLEN.  WE ARE SKEPTICAL ABOUT THE POSSIBLILITY OF A BIRD STRIKE, SINCE THERE WERE NO VISIBLE SIGNS OF BLOOD OR FEATHERS ON THE AIRCRAFT.  THE AIRLINE HAS FORWARDED THE DAMAGED WING SLAT TO BOEING FOR TESTING IN ORDER TO POSSIBLY IDENTIFY THE OBJECT THAT WAS HIT.  WE ARE SITLL AWAITING THE RESULTS OF THESE TESTS.  IF ADDITIOANL INFORMATION IS LEARNED FROM THE BOEING TESTS, WE WILL SEND AN AMENDMENT TO FAA FORM 8020-23.

20080617845339I	(-23) ON JUNE 17, 2008, AIRCRAFT N2013Z, A PIPER PA-76, RECEIVED MINOR DAMAGES WHEN IT'S NOSE GEAR COLLAPSED AFTER A SHORT FIELD LANDING.  BOTH THE INSTRUCTOR (PILOT) AND THE STUDENT REPORTED THREE GREENS, INDICATING THE MAIN AND NOSE LANDING GEARS WERE DOWN AND LOCKED.  AN EYE-WITNESS STATED THAT HE SAW THE AIRCRAFT LAND ON IT'S MAIN LANDING GEAR, ROLL FORWARD ON ALL THREE GEARS WHEN SUDDENLY THE NOSE GEAR COLLAPSED.  AN INSPECTION OF THE NOSE GEAR ACTUATOR REVEALED A DEFECTIVE ACTUATOR.  A LOCK NUT SECURES A PISTON TO THE SHAFT.  THE PISTON CAME APART FROM THE SHAFT WHEN THE LOCK NUT BROKE OFF.  WHEN THE GEAR IS DOWN AND LOCKED THERE IS NO APPLIED HYDRAULIC PRESSURE.  WHEN THE LANDING GEAR IS RETRACTED, PRESSURE IS APPLIED TO THE PISTON RETRACTING THE GEAR.  STATIC PRESSURE IS MAINTAINED ON THE ACTUATOR PISTON, KEEPING THE NOSE GEAR DOWN AND LOCKED.  WITH A DEFECTIVE ACTUATOR, THE TENSION SPRINGS CAN MAINTAIN THE NOSE GEAR DOWN AND LOCKED.  HOWEVER, SUDDEN STOP OR BUMP, WILL CAUSE THE NOSE GEAR TO COLLAPSE.  WE WERE UNABLE TO DETERMINE WHETHER THE ACTUATOR BECAME DEFECTIVE BY HARD LANDINGS OR WORN INTERNALLY.  M OR D ISSUED.

A REVIEW OF TRIP RECORDS LOCATED ON BOARD THE AIRCRAFT REVEALED THAT THE AIRCARFT HAD INITIATED ITS FIRST NORTHBOUND BANNER TOW LEG DEPARTING FROM THE ADVERTISING COMPANY'S PRIVATE GRASS STRIP AT GREEN CREEK, MIDDLE TOWNSHIP, NJ ALONG THE NEW JERSEY COAST AT 10:04 EDT AND LANDED AT LAKEWOOD, AIRPORT, LAKEWOOD, NJ (KN12) AT 12:58 EDT. AIRPORT ATTENDANTS CONFIRMED THAT THE PILOT REQUESTED TO BE TOPPED-OFF WITH FUEL AND A REVIEW OF FUEL RECORDS INDICATED THAT THE AIRCAFT WAS SERVICED WITH 27.2 GALS OF 100LL FUEL. THE PILOT, WHO HAD ACCUMULATED 500 TT SINCE BEING CERTIFICATED, DEPARTED  KN12 WITH A NEW BANNER FOR THE SOUTHBOUND LEG AT 13:47 EDT. ACCORDING THE THE PILOT STATEMENTS, THE ENGINE LOST POWER APPROXIMATELY 4 HOURS INTO THE FLIGHT AFTER TOPPING OFF WITH FUEL AT KN12. THE PILOT ALSO STATED THAT HE JETTISONED THE BANNER AND ATTEMPTED TO LAND THE AIRCRAFT IN AN OPEN FIELD, BUT REALIZED HE WAS TOO LOW AND CLIPPED A TREE DURING THE APPROACH. EYE WITNESSES STATE THAT THE PILOT ATTEMPTED A 270 DEGREE RIGHT HAND TURN AND WHILE DESCENDING BEFORE IMPACTING TERRAIN IN THE BACK YARD OF A LOCAL AREA MOTEL. EYE WITNESSES ALSO STATE THAT THE PILOT RELEASED THE BANNER OVER A TRAILER PARK ADJACENT TO THE OPEN FIELD WHERE THE PILOT WAS ATTEMPTING TO LAND. A PRELIMINARY EXAMINATION OF THE AIRPLANE INDICATED THAT BOTH MAIN 19 GALLON WING TANKS WERE FOUND TO HAVE BEEN EMPTY AND BOTH TANKS DID NOT APPEAR BREACHED BY THE IMPACT. THE FUEL SELECTOR VALVES FOR BOTH WING FUEL TANKS WERE OBSERVED POSITIONED TO THE OPEN/ON POSITION. THE PROPELLER WAS FOUND TO BE INTACT AND THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF PROPELLER ROTATION AT IMPACT. THE ENGINE TAC TIME WAS OBSERVED TO INDICATE 2683.74 HOURS IN SERVICE. THE ENTIRE AIRCRAFT AND ENGINE WERE RELOCATED TO THE OPERATOR'S FACILITIES FOR FURTHER INVESTIGATION. A POST ACCIDENT REVIEW OF MAINTENANCE RECORDS IS ALSO SCHEDULED. THE 16:54 SURFACE WEATHER OBSERVATION AT ATLANTIC CITY INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT, (KACY) REPORTED WINDS FROM THE SOUTH AT 14 KTS, GUSTING TO 21 KTS, VISIBILITY 10 MILES AND CLEAR SKIES, TEMPERATURE 82.9 DEGREES FAHRENHEIT (F), DEW POINT 57 DEGREES F, AND AN ALTIMETER SETTING OF 29.93 INCHES OF MERCURY. 20081229853579A	N360AS, PILOTED BY ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ DEPARTED RIVERSIDE AIRPORT (KRVS) IN TULSA, OK AT APPROXIMATELY 1050 CST ON DECEMBER 29, 2008.  ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ STATED THAT ALL FUEL TANKS WERE FULL AND THE FUEL SELECTOR WAS ON THE MAIN FUEL TANK WHICH IS LOCATED BEHIND THE ENGINE AND IN FRONT OF THE COCKPIT FOR THE FIRST 20 MINUTES OF THE FLIGHT.  AT THAT TIME ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ SELECTED THE LEFT FUEL TANK WHICH HE CONTINUED TO USE UNTIL THE AIRCRAFT FUEL GAUGE FOR THAT TANK INDICATED THAT 5 GALLONS HAD BEEN USED.  ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ THEN SELECTED THE RIGHT FUEL TANK UNTIL THE FUEL GAUGE INDICATED THAT HE HAD USED 10 GALLONS FROM THAT TANK.  ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ THEN MOVED THE FUEL TANK SELECTOR BACK TO THE LEFT TANK.  ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ STATED THAT APPROXIMATELY 20 MINUTES AFTER CHANGING TO THE LEFT TANK THE ENGINE FAILED.  WHILE PERFORMING THE EMERGENCY CHECKLIST THE FUEL SELECTOR WAS FOUND TO MOVE FREELY WITH LITTLE RESISTANCE.  ATTEMPTS TO RESTART THE ENGINE WERE UNSUCCESSFUL AND ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ PERFORMED A FORCED LANDING IN A FIELD APPROXIMATELY 7 MILES SOUTHWEST OF OWENSBORO AIRPORT (KOWB) IN OWENSBORO KY AT APPROXIMATELY 1300 CST. DURING THE INVESTIGATION THE MAIN FUEL TANK WAS FOUND TO HAVE ONLY A TRACE OF FUEL.  THE LEFT AND RIGHT FUEL TANKS WERE FOUND TO HAVE FUEL LEVELS THAT WERE CONSISTENT WITH ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ STATEMENTS.  INSPECTION OF THE FUEL SELECTOR FOUND THAT THE COTTER PIN USED TO CONNECT THE SELECTOR HANDLE ADAPTER TO THE SHAFT WHICH TURNS THE VALVE WAS SHEARED. THIS RESULTED IN MOVEMENT OF THE FUEL SELECTOR HANDLE NOT CHANGING THE POSITION OF THE VALVE.  THE FUEL SELECTOR VALVE WAS TESTED AND FOUND TO BE IN THE MAIN TANK POSITION.  THIS WAS ACCOMPLISHED BY ATTEMPTING TO FLOW FUEL TO THE ENGINE WHEN THE MAIN FUEL TANK WAS EMPTY, WHICH WAS UNSUCCESSFUL.  THEN AFTER ADDING A MEASURED AMOUNT OF FUEL TO THE MAIN TANK, THAT SAME AMOUNT OF FUEL WAS FLOWED TO THE ENGINE RESULTING IN THE MAIN TANK AGAIN BEING EMPTY.  INVESTIGATION CONCLUDES THAT WHILE MAKING THE CHANGE FROM THE RIGHT TANK TO THE LEFT TANK THE COTTER PIN SHEARED AS THE FUEL SELECTOR VALVED PASSED THROUGH THE MAIN TANK POSITION.  THIS RESULTED IN FUEL BEING DRAWN FROM THE MAIN TANK RATHER THEN THE LEFT TANK AS THE FUEL SELECTOR HANDLE INDICATED.  BECAUSE THE MAIN FUEL TANK HAS A CAPACITY OF ONLY 10 GALLONS, SOME OF WHICH HAD BEEN USED FOR TAKEOFF AND INITIAL CLIMB, AND THE ENGINE IN CRUISE HAS A FUEL BURN OF APPROXIMATELY 10 GALLONS PER HOUR IT DID NOT TAKE LONG FOR THAT TANK TO BE DEPLETED OF FUEL RESULTING IN THE ENGINE FAILURE.  DUE TO THE PILOTS INABILITY TO CHANGE THE POSITION OF THE FUEL SELECTOR VALVE TO ONE OF THE FUEL TANKS WHICH CONTAINED FUEL THE ATTEMPTED RESTART WAS UNSUCCESSFUL.

20090220004129I	(-23) DURING CRUISE FLIGHT FROM SPRINGFIELD, MA TO BEDFORD, MA THE AIRCRAFT DIVERTED TO WORCESTER REGIONAL AIRPORT (ORH) BECAUSE OF SMOKE IN THE COCKPIT AND CABIN.  THE COCKPIT, CABIN AND CLIMATE CONTROL SYSTEM (C4 SYSTEM) WAS ON AND WORKING PROPERLY.  ENGINE ANTI-ICE WAS TURNED ON FOR SNOW.  IMMEDIATELY THE AUTO FAIL LIGHT CAME ON FOR THE C4 SYSTEM WAS TURNED OFF.  AFTER ABOUT 30 TO 45 SECONDS, WITH THE TEMPERATURE IN THE CABIN DECREASING, THE BLEED AIR SWITCH WAS TURNED ON AND THE CABIN HEAT SWITCH SET TO LOW.  THE CABIN TEMPERATURE STABILIZED FOR ABOUT 30 SECONDS AND THEN SHOT UP TO INDICATE 75 DEGREES.  BOTH PILOT AND CO-PILOT SMELLED AND THEN SAW SMOKE IN THE COCKPIT.  THE PASSENGER REPORTED SMOKE IN CABIN.  ALL HEATING SWITCHES AND ENGINE ANTI-ICE SWITCHES WERE TURNED OFF IMMEDIATELLY.  THE SMOKE AND SMELL THEN DISSIPATED.  THE DETERMINATION WAS MADE THAT CABIN VARIABLE SIZE ORIFICE (VSO) HAD ALLOWED AN EXCESSIVE AMOUNT OF HEAT THROUGH THE DUCT WORK, OVERHEATING IT.  THIS HIGHER THAN NORMAL TEMPERATURE CAUSED THE DEBRIS, GRIME AND/OR OIL SEDIMENT TO FUME AND ENTER THE AIRCRAFT INTERIOR THROUGH THE C4 SYSTEM.  THE VSO ASSEMBLY WAS REPLACED AND ALL COMPONENTS OF THE C4 SYSTEM WERE CLEANED.

IN A DISCUSSION WITH ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^,  THE MANAGER OF RAMP TRAINING AT O?HARE, HE STATED HE HAD REMOVED THIS INDIVIDUAL?S AUTHORIZATION TO DISPATCH AIRCRAFT ON DECEMBER 18, 2008. THE PAPERWORK WAS NEVER RECEIVED BY THE TRAINING STAFF AT O?HARE.  ON ANY GIVEN DAY A ?MANPOWER SHEET? IS SUPPLIED TO THE RAMP FOR THE NEXT DAYS OPERATION SO THEY KNOW WHAT RESOURCES THEY HAVE.  THIS SHEET IS PRODUCED WITH INFORMATION FROM THE MANPOWER ADMINISTRATIVE RESOURCE SUIT (MARS) WHICH SHOWS THE QUALIFICATIONS OF  THE SCHEDULED WORK FORCE FOR THE FOLLOWING DAY.  THIS INVESTIGATION HAS DISCOVERED THAT THIS INDIVIDUAL?S MANPOWER SHEET CORRECTLY SHOWED HIM AS NOT BEING QUALIFIED TO DISPATCH AIRCRAFT.  FOR REASONS YET UNKNOWN, POSSIBLY DUE TO A SHORTAGE OF RESOURCES, THE SUPERVISORY STAFF ASSIGNED HIM TO DISPATCH AIRCRAFT ON MARCH 25, 2009, CONTRARY TO HIS STATUS IN MARS.  ON APRIL 9, 2009, AFTER OBTAINING THE FACTS OF THE CASE UNITED AIR LINES SUBMITTED A VOLUNTARY DISCLOSURE VIA THE VOLUNTARY DISCLOSURE REPORTING PROGRAM (VDRP).  THIS INCIDENT IS CLOSED.

THE ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^PILOT IN COMMAND, WHO WAS THE SOLE OCCUPANT OF THE GLIDER, WAS NOT INJURED.  ACCORDING TO THE PILOT, N61ZT WAS SELF LAUNCHED FROM GRASS ROOTS AIRPORT IN MASCOTTE, FLORIDA ON THE GLIDER?S FIRST FLIGHT AFTER BEING PURCHASED FROM THE ORIGINAL ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^BUILDER.  AT AN ALTITUDE OF APPROXIMATELY 1,800 FEET, THE ENGINE OF N61ZT EXPERIENCED A TOTAL LOSS OF POWER AND DID NOT RESPOND TO RE-START ATTEMPTS.  N61ZT WAS BEYOND GLIDING DISTANCE FROM A SUITABLE AIRPORT, WHICH RESULTED IN THE PILOT EXECUTING AN OFF AIRPORT LANDING IN A DRY LAKE BED.  A POST ACCIDENT INSPECTION OF N61ZT, CONDUCTED BY FAA INSPECTORS ON 04-10-2009, REVEALED DAMAGE TO NUMEROUS PORTIONS OF THE AIRCRAFT, TO INCLUDE, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, THE PROPELLER, LANDING GEAR, CANOPY, STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS OF THE FUSELAGE, STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS OF THE LEFT AND RIGHT WINGS, AND STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS OF THE EMPENNAGE.  A POST ACCIDENT DISASSEMBLY AND INSPECTION OF THE ROTAX 582 ENGINE INSTALLED IN N61ZT, OBSERVED BY FAA INSPECTORS ON 04-102009, REVEALED DESTRUCTION OF THE ROTARY VALVE DISC DRIVE GEAR DUE TO INSUFFICENT LUBRICATION.  SUCH GEAR FAILURE CAUSED THE ROTARY VALVE SHAFT AND ATTACHED ROTARY VALVE DISC TO CEASE ROTATION, RESULTING IN ENGINE STOPPAGE DUE TO THE INABILITY OF THE ROTARY VALVE DISC TO INTRODUCE THE AIR/FUEL MIXTURE FROM THE CARBURETORS INTO THE INTAKE PORTION OF THE ENGINE?S CYLINDERS.  INSUFFICIENT LUBRICATION OF THE ROTARY VALVE DISC DRIVE GEAR WAS DETERMINED DURING THE ENGINE DISASSEMBLY WHEN INSPECTORS OBSERVED APPROXIMATELY 2 FLUID OUNCES OF OIL DRAIN FROM THE ROTARY VALVE SHAFT ?OIL BATH? CHAMBER WHEN THE SHAFT ASSEMBLY WAS REMOVED FROM THE ENGINE CASE.  ACCORDING TO THE ROTAX INSTALLATION MANUAL, APPROXIMATELY 310CC (10.5 FLUID OUNCES) OF OIL IS REQUIRED TO FILL THE ROTARY VALVE SHAFT LUBRICATION SYSTEM.  WITH ONLY 2 FLUID OUNCES OF OIL IN THE ROTARY VALVE SHAFT ?OIL BATH? CHAMBER DURING ENGINE OPERATION, THE ROTARY VALVE  DISC DRIVE GEAR WAS SUBJECTED TO SIGNIFICANT HEAT, CAUSING CATASTROPHIC FAILURE OF THE BRASS DRIVE GEAR DUE TO INSUFFICIENT LUBRICATION.  HOWEVER, IT IS IMPORTANT TO NOTE THAT INSPECTION OF THE ENGINE COMPONENTS PRIOR TO REMOVAL AND DISASSEMBLY OF THE ENGINE FROM THE AIRFRAME OF N61ZT REVEALED THAT THE EXTERNALLY MOUNTED OIL TANK FOR THE ROTARY VALVE SHAFT LUBRICATION SYSTEM WAS FILLED TO THE PROPER LEVEL.  HOWEVER, IT IS IMPORTANT TO NOTE THAT INSPECTION OF THE ENGINE COMPONENTS PRIOR TO REMOVAL AND DISASSEMBLY OF THE ENGINE FROM THE AIRFRAME OF N61ZT REVEALED THAT THE EXTERNALLY MOUNTED OIL TANK FOR THE ROTARY VALVE SHAFT LUBRICATION SYSTEM WAS FILLED TO THE PROPER LEVEL.  INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM THE ROTAX INSTALLATION MANUAL AND FROM ROTAX SERVICE CENTER TECHNICIANS HAS SUBSTANTIATED THAT IT IS POSSIBLE FOR THE ROTARY VALVE SHAFT LUBRICATION SYSTEM EXTERNALLY MOUNTED OIL TANK TO CONTAIN A FULL QUANTITY OF OIL WITHOUT THE ROTARY VALVE SHAFT ?OIL BATH? CHAMBER WITHIN THE ENGINE CASE ACTUALLY BEING FULL OF OIL.  THIS PHENOMENON CAN OCCUR IN ROTAX 582 ENGINES MOUNTED ON AN AIRFRAME IN THE INVERTED POSITION (SPARK PLUGS DOWN) IF ROTARY VALVE SHAFT OIL IS INSTALLED WITHOUT REMOVING A VENT PLUG IN THE ENGINE CASE TO VENT THE SYSTEM DURING OIL INSTALLATION.  WITHOUT REMOVAL OF THE VENT PLUG, AN ?AIR BUBBLE? CAN FORM IN THE ROTARY VALVE SHAFT ?OIL BATH? CHAMBER, THUS PREVENTING OIL FROM FILLING THE CHAMBER.  IF THIS OCCURS, THE OIL TANK WILL INDICATE FULL, BUT INSUFFICIENT OIL WILL HAVE BEEN INTRODUCED INTO THE ROTARY VALVE SHAFT ?OIL BATH? CHAMBER, THUS CAUSING FAILURE OF THE ROTARY VALVE SHAFT BRASS DRIVE GEAR DURING ENGINE OPERATION.  THE ENGINE IN N61ZT WAS MOUNTED IN THE INVERTED POSITION, AND SUCH ENGINE WAS REINSTALLED ONTO THE AIRFRAME OF N61ZT BY THE ORIGINAL ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^BUILDER

EVERY TOWER IS CIRCLED AT LEAST TWICE COUNTER CLOCKWISE AND THEN A LANDING IS ACCOMPLISHED AND THE INSPECTOR THEN CONTINUES HIS INSPECTION OUTSIDE OF THE HELICOPTER.  AT THIS POINT IN THE POWER LINE CONSTRUCTION PROJECT ALL THREE PHASES (POWER LINES, TOWERS AND GUIDE WIRES) HAVE BEEN INSTALLED AND THEREFORE THE CLEAR CUT AREA IS NOT AS EASILY ACCESSIBLE AS EARLIER IN THE PROJECT.  DEPENDING ON THE LOCATION AND ORIENTATION OF THE POWER LINE THE TOWERS HAVE GUIDE WIRES ATTACHED TO THEM RANGING FROM ONE UP TO FOURTEEN PER TOWER.  NO TOWER STRUCTURE #102 THE PILOT STATED THAT HE FLEW ALONGSIDE THE POWER LINE AT ABOUT 25 FEET ABOVE THE WIRE.  HE APPROACHED THE TOWER AND COMPLETED TWO FULL TURNS AROUND THE TOWER.  BOTH HE AND THE INSPECTOR NOTICED ONLY ONE GUIDE WIRE LOCATED ON THE UPHILL SIDE OF THE LINE.  NO OTHER GUIDE LINES WERE IDENTIFIED BY EITHER THE INSPECTOR OR THE PILOT.  THE PILOT DESCENDED ON THE DOWNHILL SIDE OF THE TOWER TO LAND FOR THE INSPECTOR TO CONDUCT HIS GROUND INSPECTION.  DURING HIS DESCENT AT ABOUT 15-20 FEET ABOVE THE GROUND AND A GROUND SPEED OF A SLOW WALKING PACE ONE OF THE HELICOPTERS ROTOR BLADES CAME INTO CONTACT WITH AN UNSEEN GUIDE WIRE. 20091129052032I	ON 11/29/09, AT APPROXIMATELY 07:09 MST, A FEDX DC-10 TAXIING NORTH ON H CLIPPED THE RIGHT WINGLET OF A SWAA B-737.  THE TOP HALF OF THE WINGLET WAS SEVERED OFF OF THE 737 AND THE DC-10 INCURRED MINOR DAMAGE TO THE LEADING EDGE OF THE LEFT WING SLAT APPROXIMATELY 4-5 FEET INBOARD .PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT THE SWAA #5506 REQUESTED A PUSH-BACK CLEARANCE AT GATE B13 FROM SLC ATCT.  THEY WERE INSTRUCTED "CLEARED TO PUSH, START ENGINES YOUR DISCRETION, ADVISE READY TO TAXI".  THE TUG OPERATOR PUSHED THE AIRCRAFT BACK TO AN AREA WHICH AFFORDED CLEARANCE FOR THE WINGS TO CLEAR ANY OBSTACLES AT WHICH TIME THE AIRCRAFT WAS TURNED APPROXIMATELY 90 DEGREES WHICH PLACED THE NOSE OF THE AIRCRAFT HEADING NORTH.  HOWEVER, THIS POSITION LEFT THE NOSE WHEEL ON THE LINE WHICH SEPARATES THE NON-MOVEMENT AREA (RAMP) AND TAXIWAY H. THIS PLACED THE RIGHT HALF OF THE FUSELAGE AND THE RIGHT WING PORTRUDING INTO TAXIWAY H.  APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER SWAA WAS ISSUED THE PUSH BACK A FEDX DC-10, FLIGHT #FDX 876 WAS CLEARED FROM THE SOUTH CARGO RAMP TO 16L VIA H.   AS THE DC-10 APPROACHED THE 737 THE CREW WAS UNAWARE THAT THE LEFT WING OF THE DC-10 DID NOT HAVE ENOUGH CLEARANCE TO MISS THE RIGHT WING OF THE 737 AND THE WINGLET ON THE 737 WAS CUT-OFF.  THE DC-10 CREW WAS UNAWARE OF THE INCIDENT UNTIL THE SWAA CREW REPORTED IT TO ATC.  THE DC-10 WAS THEN INSTRUCTED TO PROCEED TO RWY 16L AND RETURN TO THE FEDX RAMP.  THE VISUAL CONDITIONS WERE VMC BUT IT WAS FAIRLY DARK WHICH LEFT THE DC-10 CREW WITH IMPAIRED VISION.  THEY KNEW THAT THEY HAD THE CLEARANCE FOR H AND THAT ATC WOULD NOT ALLOW THEM TO PROCEED WITH THE TAXI IF THERE WAS ANYTHING THAT WOULD RESULT IN AN INCIDENT, SUCH AS OCCURRED.THE INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THE ATCT WAS UNAWARE THAT, IN MANY INSTANCES, THE SWAA 737 MUST ENTER TAXI-WAY H, TO SOME EXTENT OR ANOTHER, IN ORDER TO HAVE THE CLEARANCE TO SWING THE AIRCRAFT INTO A POSITION TO REQUEST AND PROCEED FOR TAXI ON H.POST INCIDENT, SWAA, SLC ATCT AND SLC AIRPORTS, HAVE DEVELOPED A NEW PROCEDURE TO PREVENT A REOCCURRANCE OF THIS TYPE OF INCIDENT.  BASICALLY, SWAA HAS PUBLISHED INSTRUCTIONS TO THEIR CREWS THAT THEY MUST REQUEST A PUSH CLEARANCE AND TO EXPECT SOME DELAY PRIOR TO PUSH IF ANOTHER AIRCRAFT IS ON H AT WHICH TIME ATC WILL CLEAR THEM TO PUSH.DUE TO THE POSSIBLE CONFUSION ON THE PART OF THE SWAA CREW AND THE FEDX CREW AND THE LIMITED VISION PRESENT AT THE TIME AND THE SWAA CREWS BEING HANDLED AND PUSHED AS WAS CUSTOMERY FROM PAST PRACTICE, IT WAS DETERMINED NOT APPRORIATE TO VIOLATE THE CREWS OR OPERATORS. TOTAL PILOT TIME IN THE LAST YEAR HAS BEEN REQUESTED AND WILL FILE AN AMENDMENT IF IT IS RECEIVED.THIS REPORT IS RELATED TO SLC ATCT REPORT, #SLC-ATCT-031 AND SLC AIRPORT POLICE REPORT #210407.
